source.title: Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms
source.authors: James Newton and Jack A. Thorne
readSections: The published version, read in full: the open-access (CC BY 4.0) PDF from pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-021-00127-3.pdf (116 pages; SHA-256 ef76912a84fdf3d0630fe3aaa83548110f9aca9fc50a421401ba5462512dce37; fetched 23 September 2026; received 17 July 2020, revised 22 September 2021, accepted 25 September 2021, online 15 October 2021). Read: the Introduction (Theorems A, B, D, E, Corollary C), §1 (definite unitary groups, endoscopy, Mœglin's L-packets, depth-zero types for U_3 and GL_n, fixed-type lifting rings, algebraic modular forms), Part I — §2 (trianguline deformations, pseudocharacter spaces, Emerton's eigenvariety, Theorems 2.24, 2.27, Corollary 2.28, Lemmas 2.29–2.30, the eigencurve, Theorem 2.33, Lemmas 2.34–2.35) and §3 (Buzzard–Kilford and ping pong, Theorem 3.1), Part II — §4 (Theorem 4.1, Proposition 4.6), §5 (Theorems 5.2 and 5.7, Proposition 5.8), §6 (Theorem 6.1), §7 (Theorem 7.1, Proposition 7.4, Theorems 7.6–7.7) and §8 (Theorem 8.1, Propositions 8.2–8.3, Lemma 8.4), and the references. Page numbers are the journal's; misprints were checked on page images.
arXiv 1912.11261 v3 (27 September 2021) is the version the journal published; the published text was the one extracted.

Cited inputs were not read; items resting on them (Labesse, Mœglin, Moy–Prasad, Lust–Stevens, Kazhdan–Varshavsky, Geck, Dudas–Malle, Shotton, Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao, Bellaïche–Chenevier, Nakamura, Emerton, Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen, Breuil, Orlik–Strauch, Chenevier, Geraghty, Buzzard–Kilford, Coleman, Allen–Newton–Thorne, Thorne, Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor, Anastassiades–Thorne, Newton–Thorne 2020, Diamond, Diamond–Taylor, Kisin, Thorne 2016, Khare–Thorne, Weston) state them as the paper uses them.

summary: For every level-one cuspidal Hecke eigenform f and every n ≥ 1 the paper proves that Sym^n f is automorphic (Theorem A). It extends this to every non-CM eigenform whose local components are nowhere supercuspidal (Theorem B), which includes semistable elliptic curves, and deduces that their completed symmetric power L-functions are entire (Corollary C). The proof has two halves. Theorem D shows that automorphy of Sym^{n−1} spreads along irreducible components of eigenvarieties. It rests on trianguline deformation theory on Emerton's eigenvariety for a definite unitary group, the vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups (Newton–Thorne 2020) and classicality via companion points. A game of 'ping pong' on the Buzzard–Kilford annuli of the tame-level-1, 2-adic eigencurve then connects all level-one forms. Theorem E produces one level-one form with automorphic Sym^{n−1}. It starts from the CM form of weight 5 and level 4, raises the level on definite unitary groups with a congruence of depth-zero types of U_3, and applies Galois deformation theory for residually reducible representations (Allen–Newton–Thorne) and Anastassiades–Thorne. Theorem B kills ramification by analytic continuation and a patching argument. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 already plans the endpoints with Newton–Thorne as source. The method goes to one new Part II of that roadmap (analytic continuation of functoriality along eigenvarieties) and to five pending candidates, with which it coalesces: Clozel–Thorne's unitary level-raising Part II, the eigenvariety and trianguline owners of Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen and Ding, Fintzen's types Part II, and Boxer–Calegari–Gee's polarized automorphy lifting Part II. Four misprints are recorded.

items.name: Theorem A (Theorem 7.7): symmetric powers of level-one eigenforms
items.statement: Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of level 1 (everywhere unramified). Then for each integer n ≥ 2 the symmetric power lifting Sym^{n−1} π exists, as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_ℚ); equivalently (Theorem 7.7), for n ≥ 3, weight k ≥ 2 and any ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, Sym^{n−1} r_{π,ι} is automorphic.
items.locator: Introduction, Theorem A, p. 2; §7, Theorem 7.7, p. 104
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 plans exactly this: it is to 'integrate Newton–Thorne source-scoped symmetric-power automorphy', and Newton–Thorne is its selected source. The proof machinery is routed to the Part IIs below. Theorem A = Theorem D (Theorem 3.1) + Theorem E (Theorem 7.6).

items.name: Theorem B (Theorem 8.1): symmetric powers when no local component is supercuspidal
items.statement: Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 and conductor N ≥ 1 which does not have CM (no quadratic Hecke character χ with π ≅ π ⊗ χ). Suppose that for each prime l | N the Jacquet module of π_l is non-trivial (π_l is not supercuspidal; equivalently π_l admits an accessible refinement). Then for each n ≥ 2 the symmetric power lifting Sym^{n−1} π exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_ℚ). This covers all non-CM newforms of level Γ_1(N) with N squarefree, in particular those of semistable elliptic curves.
items.locator: Introduction, Theorem B, p. 2; §8, Theorem 8.1, p. 104
items.note: Planned in ML.3 (as Theorem A). Proved by killing ramification (Propositions 8.2–8.3, routed to the analytic-continuation Part II) and a final residually irreducible automorphy lifting step (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1). The sequel PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B removes the hypothesis on π_l.

items.name: Corollary C: analytic continuation of symmetric power L-functions of semistable elliptic curves
items.statement: Let E be a semistable elliptic curve over ℚ. Then for each n ≥ 2 the completed symmetric power L-function Λ(Sym^n E, s) (as defined e.g. by Dummigan–Martin–Watkins) admits an analytic continuation to the entire complex plane.
items.note: ML.3 plans the analytic consequences of Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy; meromorphic continuation was already known from potential automorphy (BLGHT11), and the paper remarks that automorphy makes effective Sato–Tate possible.

items.name: Theorem D (Theorem 3.1): symmetric power functoriality propagates through level one
items.statement: Fix n ≥ 2. Let π_0 be an everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 such that Sym^{n−1} r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic for some (equivalently any) prime p and ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. Then Sym^{n−1} r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every everywhere unramified cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight l ≥ 2.
items.locator: Introduction, Theorem D, p. 3; §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 61 (proof p. 65)
items.note: Proved by playing 'ping pong' on the Buzzard–Kilford annuli of the tame level 1, 2-adic eigencurve (Lemmas 3.6–3.7) using Theorem 2.33.

items.name: Theorem E (Theorem 7.6): existence of one level-one form with automorphic symmetric power
items.statement: For each n ≥ 3 there is a cuspidal, everywhere unramified automorphic representation π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 such that, for any isomorphism ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, Sym^{n−1} r_{π,ι} is automorphic.
items.locator: Introduction, Theorem E, p. 4; §7, Theorem 7.6, pp. 103–104
items.note: Proof: Corollary 7.3 gives a weight-5 form σ, Steinberg at q ≡ 3 mod 4 and with χ_2 of conductor 4 at 2, with Sym^{n−1} automorphic; Theorem 2.33 on the q-adic tame-level-4 eigencurve moves to σ′ unramified outside 2 of weight k ≡ 3 mod 4; since Buzzard–Kilford leaves no level-4 newforms of odd slope, its 2-adic refinements are n-regular and Theorem 2.33 on the tame-level-1 2-adic eigencurve gives an everywhere unramified π.

items.name: Tate-normalised local Langlands correspondence, Sp_n(ψ) and St_n(ψ)
items.statement: For K/ℚ_l finite, rec_K is the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(K) and rec^T_K(π) = rec_K(π ⊗ |·|^{(1−n)/2}). For a smooth character ψ, Sp_n(ψ) = (r, N) is the Weil–Deligne representation r = ⊕_{i=1}^n ψ|·|^{1−i} ∘ Art_K^{−1} with N e_1 = 0, N e_{i+1} = e_i, and St_n(ψ) is the unique irreducible quotient of Ind^{GL_n(K)}_{B_n(K)} ψ ∘ det; rec^T_K(St_n(ψ)) = Sp_n(ψ). π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ π_k denotes the representation with rec(⊞π_i) = ⊕ rec(π_i).
items.note: The characteristic-zero local correspondence for GL_m with full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters and monodromy is ET.6.

items.name: Galois representations of polarizable regular algebraic cuspidal representations
items.statement: If F is CM or totally real and π is a cuspidal, regular algebraic, polarizable automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ, then for any ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ there is a continuous semisimple r_{π,ι} : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) with WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{F_v}(ι^{−1}π_v) for every finite place v, de Rham at v | p with τ-Hodge–Tate weights {λ_{ιτ,1} + (n − 1), λ_{ιτ,2} + (n − 2), …, λ_{ιτ,n}} (the cyclotomic character has weight −1); purity of WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}}) (Caraiani) makes it generic.
items.locator: Notation, p. 8; §2, proof of Theorem 2.24, p. 47
items.note: The polarized characteristic-zero Galois realisation is AG2.2 and local–global compatibility with monodromy (Caraiani, Taylor–Yoshida) is AG2.5.

items.name: The quasi-split unitary groups U_n and their Levi subgroups
items.statement: For E/F quadratic, θ_n(g) = Φ_n c(g)^{−t} Φ_n^{−1} with Φ_n = antidiag(1, −1, …, (−1)^{n−1}); U_n ⊂ Res_{E/F} GL_n is the fixed subgroup, quasi-split with the θ-invariant standard pinning, extended to a group scheme over 𝒪_F; ^LU_n = GL_n(ℂ) ⋊ W_F with w_c · g = Φ_n g^{−t} Φ_n^{−1}. For 2(n_1 + ⋯ + n_{k−1}) + n_k = n, M_{(n_1,…,n_k)} ≅ (Res GL_{n_1} × ⋯ × Res GL_{n_{k−1}}) × U_{n_k} with parabolic Q_{(n_1,…,n_k)}, and π_1 × ⋯ × π_k = i^{U_n}_Q π_1 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ π_k.
items.note: Basic set-up of the unitary groups whose L-packets and types are used in §§1.8–4.

items.name: Standard assumptions and the definite unitary group G_n with its pure inner twist
items.statement: Standard assumptions: F is a CM field with F/F⁺ everywhere unramified (so [F⁺ : ℚ] is even), p a prime, S ⊇ S_p a finite set of finite places of F⁺ all split in F, with chosen factorisations v = ṽṽ^c. G = G_n over F⁺ has G(R) = {g ∈ GL_n(R ⊗_{F⁺} F) : g = (1 ⊗ c)(g)^{−t}} (1.0.1): quasi-split at finite places, compact at infinity, a reductive group scheme over 𝒪_{F⁺}. The inner twist ξ : U_{n,F} → G_F, ξ(g_1, g_2) = (g_1, Φ_n^{−1}g_2Φ_n), is lifted to a pure inner twist (ξ, u) (u_c = (Φ_n, Φ_n) for n odd; (ζΦ_n, ζ^{−1}Φ_n) with tr ζ = 0 for n even); μ_F is a character of F^×\𝔸_F^× with μ|_{𝔸_{F⁺}^×} = δ_{F/F⁺} ∘ Art, unramified at inert places. These give conjugacy classes of isomorphisms ι_v : G(F⁺_v) → U_n(F⁺_v) (v finite) and ι_w : G(F⁺_v) → GL_n(F_w) (v = ww^c split), and the construction is compatible with base change to totally real L⁺/F⁺.
items.note: The triviality of u in H¹(F⁺_v, U_n) at every finite place uses Hilbert 90 and Rogawski §1.9.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.3: base change from G to GL_n and its Galois representations
items.statement: Let σ be an automorphic representation of G(𝔸_{F⁺}). There are a partition n = n_1 + ⋯ + n_k and discrete conjugate self-dual automorphic representations π_i of GL_{n_i}(𝔸_F) such that π = π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ π_k satisfies: (1) at finite places where σ is unramified, π_w is the unramified base change of σ_{w|F⁺}; (2) at split v = ww^c, π_w ≅ σ_v ∘ ι_w^{−1}; (3) at v | ∞, π_v has the infinitesimal character of ⊗_τ W_τ with σ_v ≅ W_τ|_{G(F⁺_v)} (Labesse Corollaire 5.3). σ is ι-ordinary if π is (Geraghty Definition 5.3). Corollary 1.3: there is a unique continuous semisimple r_{σ,ι} : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p), unramified at prime-to-p places where σ is unramified, de Rham at ṽ | p, with WD(r_{σ,ι}|_{G_{F_w}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(σ_v ∘ ι_w^{−1}) at split places. If r_{σ,ι}|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is multiplicity free, each π_i is cuspidal and π is tempered.
items.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.2, Corollary 1.3 and the remark after it, pp. 11–12
items.note: Unitary-to-GL_n base change is ET.7a (from the stable and twisted trace formulas of ET.4, with Moeglin–Waldspurger's residual spectrum), and AG2.2 attaches the Galois representations to the discrete constituents.

items.name: Theorem 1.4: descent from GL_n to G
items.statement: Let π be a RACSDC (regular algebraic, conjugate self-dual, cuspidal) automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) unramified outside S. Then there is an automorphic representation σ of G(𝔸_{F⁺}) with σ_v^{ι_v^{−1}(U_n(𝒪_{F⁺_v}))} ≠ 0 for each finite v ∉ S and with base change π (Labesse Théorème 5.4).
items.note: Unitary descent is part of ET.7a's base-change exports.

items.name: Endoscopic data, transfer factors and transfer for G and for twisted Res GL_n
items.statement: Equivalence classes of endoscopic data for G correspond to (p, q) with p + q = n, p ≥ q ≥ 0, represented by extended triples (H = U_p × U_q, s = diag(1_p, −1_q), η) with η built from μ^{(−1)^q}, μ^{(−1)^p}; local transfer factors are normalised (n odd) by the Whittaker normalisation of the quasi-split U_n (= Langlands–Shelstad Δ_0) transported by the pure inner twist, satisfying the adelic product formula (Kaletha); every f ∈ C_c^∞ admits a transfer f^H (Waldspurger, Laumon–Ngô). For twisted Res_{F/F⁺}GL_n ⋊ θ_n the principal triple (U_n, 1, η) with trivial transfer factors gives f ↦ f̃ and every function on U_n(F⁺_v) arises (Labesse Lemme 4.1); M_H = Res GL_p × GL_q with its twisted space M̃_H.
items.note: Endoscopic data are ET.0, Langlands–Shelstad and Kottwitz–Shelstad transfer factors ET.1, the fundamental lemma and existence of transfer ET.3. The specific normalisation through the pure inner twist is carried by Propositions 1.6–1.7.

items.name: Proposition 1.6: archimedean endoscopic character identities with a sign
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 be odd, v | ∞ a place of F⁺, E = (H, s, η) an extended endoscopic triple and φ_H : W_{F⁺_v} → ^LH a Langlands parameter such that η ∘ φ_H is the parameter of an irreducible σ_v of G(F⁺_v); let π be the (tempered, θ-invariant) representation of H(F_ṽ) with parameter φ_H|_{W_{F_v}} and f_v a coefficient for σ_v. Then there is a sign ϵ(v, E, φ_H) ∈ {±1} with π̃(f̃^H_v) = ϵ(v, E, φ_H)σ_v(f_v) = ϵ(v, E, φ_H), the twisted trace Whittaker-normalised; and ϵ(v, E_{L⁺}, φ_H|_{W_{L⁺_v}}) = ϵ(v|_{F⁺}, E, φ_H) for L⁺/F⁺ totally real.
items.locator: §1.5, Proposition 1.6 and the remark after it, p. 14
items.note: Proof: Clozel 1982 and Kaletha 2016 Proposition 5.10. The sign depends on the pure inner twist.

items.name: Proposition 1.7: unramified and split endoscopic character identities on the nose
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 be odd, v finite, f_v ∈ C_c^∞(G(F⁺_v)), E = (H, s, η). (1) If v is inert and f_v unramified, then for an unramified parameter φ_H with σ_{v,H}, σ_v, π of parameters φ_H, η ∘ φ_H, φ_H|_{W_{F_ṽ}}: π̃(f̃^H_v) = σ_{v,H}(f^H_v) = σ_v(f_v), the twisted trace normalised so that θ fixes the spherical vector (Whittaker-normalised if π is generic). (2) If v splits, the same identities hold for bounded parameters with the Whittaker-normalised twisted trace.
items.note: Proof: the fundamental lemmas for stable base change (Clozel 1990; Rogawski Proposition 4.13.2 in the split case) and standard endoscopy (Laumon–Ngô) with Hales's canonical normalisation; in the split case constant terms (Rogawski Lemma 4.13.1, Shin §§3.3–3.4).

items.name: Conjugate self-dual parameters extending to ^LU_n; θ-discrete representations
items.statement: At a place v of F⁺ inert in F, A(GL_n(F_ṽ)) is identified with Langlands parameters φ : W_{F_ṽ} × SL_2(ℂ) → GL_n(ℂ), A_t with the tempered ones and A^θ with the conjugate self-dual ones. A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺ is the set of φ extending to φ_{F⁺_v} : W_{F⁺_v} × SL_2(ℂ) → ^LU_n (unique up to conjugacy, GGP Theorem 8.1). Writing φ = ⊕ρ_i^{l_i} ⊕ σ_j^{m_j} ⊕ (τ_k ⊕ τ_k^{w_c,∨})^{n_k} with ρ_i conjugate self-dual of sign (−1)^{n−1} and σ_j of sign (−1)^n, the extension exists iff every m_j is even; it is discrete iff all l_i = 1 and J, K are empty, and then π is θ-discrete.

items.name: Supercuspidal support
items.statement: S_n is the set of formal sums of supercuspidal representations π_i of GL_{n_i}(F_ṽ) with Σn_i = n, and every π ∈ A(GL_n(F_ṽ)) has a supercuspidal support sc(π) ∈ S_n: π is a subquotient of π_1 × ⋯ × π_k (Bernstein–Zelevinsky).
items.note: The subquotient description by supercuspidal support is SR.3.

items.name: Proposition 1.9: Mœglin's extended cuspidal support determines a base change
items.statement: Mœglin attaches to τ ∈ A_t(U_n(F⁺_v)) an extended cuspidal support esc(τ) ∈ S_n (reduced to the supercuspidal case by esc(τ) = Σsc(π_i) + esc(τ_0) + Σsc(π_i^θ) for τ a subquotient of π_1 × ⋯ × π_{k−1} × τ_0). Then there is a unique π_τ ∈ A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺ with esc(τ) = sc(π_τ).
items.note: Proof: Mœglin 2007 Lemme 5.4 and Théorème 5.7 (square-integrable case), reduced via Waldspurger's Proposition III.4.1.

items.name: Proposition 1.10: stable base change BC and the L-packets Π(π)
items.statement: The map BC : A_t(U_n(F⁺_v)) → A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺, τ ↦ π_τ, is surjective with finite fibres; the L-packets Π(π) = BC^{−1}(π) partition A_t(U_n(F⁺_v)).
items.note: Mœglin 2007 Théorème 5.7 for θ-discrete π, then reduction.

items.name: Proposition 1.11: twisted character identity for Π(π)
items.statement: Let π ∈ A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺ with an extension π̃ to GL_n(F_ṽ) ⋊ θ. There are constants c_τ ∈ ℂ^× such that π̃(f) = Σ_{τ∈Π(π)} c_τ τ(f^{U_n}) for every f ∈ C_c^∞(GL_n(F_ṽ) ⋊ θ).
items.note: Proof: Mœglin 2007 Proposition 5.5 (θ-discrete), constant terms (Morel Lemma 6.3.4) and disjointness of Jordan–Hölder factors (Waldspurger Proposition III.4.1).

items.name: Depth-zero cuspidal representations of U_3(k(v)) and GL_3(k(ṽ))
items.statement: τ(v) is the unique cuspidal unipotent representation of U_3(k(v)) (Lusztig 1977 §9). For k_3/k(v) cubic, C = ker(N : Res_{k_3k(ṽ)/k(v)}𝔾_m → Res_{k_3/k(v)}𝔾_m) embeds uniquely up to conjugacy in U_3 (Deligne–Lusztig Corollary 1.14); for p with q_v a primitive 6th root of unity mod p and θ : C(k(v)) → ℂ^× of order p, λ(v, θ) = −R^{U_3}_C θ is cuspidal irreducible (C lies in no proper rational parabolic). With C̃ = Res_{k_3k(ṽ)/k(ṽ)}𝔾_m and θ̃(z) = θ(z/z^c), λ̃(ṽ, θ̃) = R^{GL_3}_{C̃} θ̃ is a cuspidal irreducible representation of GL_3(k(ṽ)).
items.note: Deligne–Lusztig theory of finite groups of Lie type is not planned in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 1.12(1): the supercuspidal τ_v and its base change
items.statement: Assume k(v) has odd characteristic. τ_v = c-Ind^{U_3(F⁺_v)}_{U_3(𝒪_{F⁺_v})} τ(v) is a supercuspidal irreducible admissible representation of U_3(F⁺_v) and BC(τ_v) = St_2(χ) ⊞ 1 with χ : F_ṽ^× → ℂ^× the non-trivial unramified quadratic character.
items.note: Proof: Moy–Prasad Proposition 6.6 (supercuspidality); reducibility points of depth-zero supercuspidals (Lust–Stevens §8, odd residue characteristic) give Red(τ_v) = {(1, 3/2), (χ, 1)} or {(1, 1), (χ, 3/2)}; the sign condition BC(τ_v) ∈ A^θ_t⁺ selects the second.

items.name: Proposition 1.12(2)–(3): λ_v(θ), its GL_3 counterpart and its base change
items.statement: λ_v(θ) = c-Ind^{U_3(F⁺_v)}_{U_3(𝒪)} λ(v, θ) is supercuspidal irreducible; extending λ̃(ṽ, θ̃) trivially on F_ṽ^×, λ̃_ṽ(θ̃) = c-Ind^{GL_3(F_ṽ)}_{F_ṽ^×GL_3(𝒪_{F_ṽ})} λ̃(ṽ, θ̃) is a supercuspidal irreducible representation of GL_3(F_ṽ) and BC(λ_v(θ)) = λ̃_ṽ(θ̃).
items.note: Red(λ_v(θ)) = {(ρ, 1)} with ρ a conjugate self-dual unramified twist of λ̃_ṽ(θ̃).

items.name: Corollary 1.13: a member of the L-packet containing τ_v
items.statement: Let n = 2k + 1 and π = St_2(χ) ⊞ 1 ⊞ (⊞_{i=1}^{2k−2} χ_i) ∈ A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺ with χ the non-trivial unramified quadratic character and each χ_i|_{𝒪^×} of order 2. After relabelling χ_i = χ_{2k−1−i}^{w_c,∨} (i = 1, …, k − 1), and Π(π) contains every irreducible subquotient of χ_1 × ⋯ × χ_{k−1} × τ_v.
items.note: Π(π) is not claimed to contain only these, even for k = 1.

items.name: Depth-zero unrefined minimal K-types (Moy–Prasad)
items.statement: For a parahoric subgroup (here p_v ⊂ U_n(𝒪_{F⁺_v}) of type (1, …, 1, 3), the preimage of Q_{(1,…,1,3)}(k(v))) with reductive quotient M(k(v)) and a cuspidal representation σ(v) of M(k(v)), the pair (p_v, σ(v)) is a depth-zero unrefined minimal K-type; E(σ(v)) is the set of irreducible representations of (F_ṽ^×)^{k−1} × U_3(𝒪) restricting to σ(v) on M(𝒪).
items.note: The Moy–Prasad filtration and depth are in the types Part II proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21.

items.name: Proposition 1.14(1): compact induction from a depth-zero type
items.statement: For a cuspidal irreducible σ(v) of M_{(1,…,1,3)}(k(v)) and σ′ ∈ E(σ(v)), c-Ind^{M(F⁺_v)}_{(F_ṽ^×)^{k−1}×U_3(𝒪)} σ′ is irreducible and supercuspidal.
items.note: Moy–Prasad Proposition 6.6.

items.name: Proposition 1.14(2): representations containing a depth-zero type
items.statement: An irreducible admissible representation π of U_n(F⁺_v) has π|_{p_v} ⊇ σ(v) iff π is a subquotient of i^{U_n}_{Q_{(1,…,1,3)}} c-Ind σ′ for some σ′ ∈ E(σ(v)).
items.note: Moy–Prasad Theorem 6.11.

items.name: The types τ(v, n) and λ(v, θ, n) of p_v
items.statement: With ω(ṽ) the non-trivial quadratic character of k(ṽ)^× (odd characteristic), τ(v, n) (resp. λ(v, θ, n)) is the representation of p_v inflated from ω(ṽ) ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ ω(ṽ) ⊗ τ(v) (resp. ⊗ λ(v, θ)) of M_{(1,…,1,3)}(k(v)); for λ one assumes q_v mod p a primitive 6th root of unity and θ of order p. φ(v, θ, n) ∈ C_c^∞(U_n(F⁺_v)) is supported on p_v and inflated from the character of λ(v, θ, n)^∨, so π(φ) is a positive multiple of dim Hom_{p_v}(λ(v, θ, n), π|_{p_v}).

items.name: Proposition 1.15(1): modular irreducibility of the cuspidal unipotent type
items.statement: Via a fixed Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, the reduction τ̄(v, n) of τ(v, n) is irreducible.
items.note: Dudas–Malle 2018 (modular irreducibility of cuspidal unipotent characters).

items.name: Proposition 1.15(2): a congruence of types
items.statement: If q_v mod p is a primitive 6th root of unity, the semisimplified reduction λ̄(v, θ, n) contains τ̄(v, n) as a Jordan–Hölder factor with multiplicity 1.
items.note: A Brauer-character computation for U_3(k(v)) (Geck 1990 Theorem 4.2; the paper notes a typo in Geck's proof).

items.name: Proposition 1.16: endoscopic transfer of the test function φ(v, θ, n)
items.statement: Assume char k(v) > n. Let φ = φ(v, θ, n), E = (H, s, η) with H = U_p × U_q, and π_p ∈ A^θ_t(GL_p(F_ṽ))⁺, π_q ∈ A^θ_t(GL_q(F_ṽ))⁺ with (π_p ⊗ π_q)~(φ̃^H) ≠ 0. Then sc(π_p) + sc(π_q) = λ̃_ṽ(θ̃) + χ_1 + ⋯ + χ_{2k−2} with each χ_i|_{𝒪^×} = ω(ṽ).
items.note: Proof: Proposition 1.11 with Kazhdan–Varshavsky Theorem 2.2.6 (endoscopic transfer of Deligne–Lusztig functions, the reason for char k(v) > n), transitivity of Deligne–Lusztig induction and Proposition 1.14.

items.name: Proposition 1.18: representations of GL_{n_1} containing the Deligne–Lusztig type λ̃(ṽ, Θ)
items.statement: Let q_ṽ mod p be a primitive n_1-th root of unity, Θ : k_{n_1}^× → ℂ^× of order p and λ̃(ṽ, Θ) = (−1)^{n_1−1}R^{GL_{n_1}}_{Res 𝔾_m} Θ (irreducible). For π irreducible admissible of GL_{n_1}(F_ṽ) the following are equivalent: (1) π|_{GL_{n_1}(𝒪)} contains λ̃(ṽ, Θ); (2) there is χ : F_{ṽ,n_1}^× → ℂ^× with χ|_{𝒪^×} = Θ and rec_{F_ṽ}(π) ≅ Ind^{W_{F_ṽ}}_{W_{F_{ṽ,n_1}}}(χ ∘ Art^{−1}); in particular π is supercuspidal.
items.note: Henniart 1992 §3.4 (explicit unramified Langlands–Kazhdan correspondence) and Moy–Prasad.

items.name: Proposition 1.19: representations of GL_n containing λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n) on r_ṽ
items.statement: With q_ṽ, r_ṽ ⊂ GL_n(𝒪) the parahorics of types (n_1, n_2) and (n_1, 1, …, 1) and λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n) inflated from λ̃(ṽ, Θ) ⊗ (ω(ṽ) ∘ det): π|_{r_ṽ} contains λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n)|_{r_ṽ} iff sc(π) = π_1 + χ_1 + ⋯ + χ_{n_2} with π_1 as in Proposition 1.18 and each χ_i|_{𝒪^×} = ω(ṽ).
items.note: Moy–Prasad.

items.name: Proposition 1.20: representations of GL_n containing λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n) on q_ṽ
items.statement: For π irreducible admissible of GL_n(F_ṽ): π|_{q_ṽ} contains λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n) iff π = π_1 ⊞ π_2 with π_1|_{GL_{n_1}(𝒪)} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ) and π_2|_{GL_{n_2}(𝒪)} ⊇ ω(ṽ) ∘ det (so π_2 is a ramified quadratic twist of an unramified representation), although (q_ṽ, λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n)) is not a type unless n_2 = 1.
items.note: Proof: π^{λ̃} → π_{N_P}^{λ̃_{N_P}} is an isomorphism (Vignéras II.10.1, Morris Lemma 3.6), then the geometric lemma (Bernstein–Zelevinsky 2.12) and Zelevinsky Proposition 8.5.

items.name: Lemma 1.21: splitting of lifts of ρ̄_ṽ = σ̄_1 ⊕ σ̄_2
items.statement: Let ρ̄_ṽ = σ̄_{ṽ,1} ⊕ σ̄_{ṽ,2} with σ̄_{ṽ,1} ≅ Ind^{G_{F_ṽ}}_{G_{F_{ṽ,n_1}}} ψ̄_ṽ (ψ̄_ṽ unramified) and σ̄_{ṽ,2} ⊗ ω(ṽ) ∘ Art^{−1} unramified on inertia. Every lift ρ_ṽ to R ∈ 𝒞_𝒪 is (1 + M_n(m_R))-conjugate to σ_{ṽ,1} ⊕ σ_{ṽ,2} with σ_{ṽ,i} lifting σ̄_{ṽ,i}, each unique up to (1 + M_{n_i}(m_R))-conjugacy.
items.note: H⁰ and H¹ of Hom(σ̄_1, σ̄_2) and Hom(σ̄_2, σ̄_1) vanish (Shotton Lemma 2.3).

items.name: Proposition 1.22(1)–(2): the fixed-inertial-type lifting ring R(ṽ, Θ, ρ̄_ṽ)
items.statement: R(ṽ, Θ, ρ̄_ṽ) is the quotient of the universal lifting ring R^□_ṽ attached (Shotton Definition 3.5) to the inertial type τ_ṽ = ⊕_{i=1}^{n_1}(ι^{−1}Θ^{q_ṽ^{i−1}} ∘ Art^{−1}) ⊕ (ω(ṽ) ∘ Art^{−1})^{⊕n_2}. (1) It is reduced, p-torsion-free, supported on a union of irreducible components of R^□_ṽ, 𝒪-flat and equidimensional of dimension 1 + n². (2) A Q̄_p-point x factors through it iff σ_{x,1} ≅ Ind ψ_x with ψ_x|_I ∘ Art = ι^{−1}Θ and σ_{x,2}|_I ⊗ ω(ṽ) ∘ Art^{−1} trivial.
items.note: Fixed inertial-type deformation conditions away from p, with dimension and components, are R08.2 (Shotton Proposition 3.6).

items.name: Proposition 1.22(3)–(4): Frobenius and restriction properties of R(ṽ, Θ, ρ̄_ṽ)
items.statement: (3) There is α_ṽ ∈ R(ṽ, Θ, ρ̄_ṽ)/(ϖ) with det(X − σ_{ṽ,1}(φ_ṽ^{n_1})) ≡ (X − α_ṽ)^{n_1} mod ϖ for every Frobenius lift φ_ṽ. (4) For L_ṽ/F_ṽ finite with τ_ṽ|_{I_{L_ṽ}} trivial, R^□_{L_ṽ} → R(ṽ, Θ, ρ̄_ṽ) factors through the unramified quotient R^{ur}_{L_ṽ}.
items.note: Used in Proposition 5.6 and Lemma 6.7.

items.name: Algebraic modular forms S_λ(U, M) on G
items.statement: For a coefficient field E ⊂ Q̄_p containing all embeddings of F, λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Ĩ_p}, V_λ (Geraghty's W_λ, a tensor product of highest weight representations restricted to ∏_{v∈S_p}GL_n(F_ṽ)) with 𝒪-lattice 𝒱_λ (Geraghty's M_λ), U = ∏U_v open compact with U_v ⊂ ι_ṽ^{−1}GL_n(𝒪) at v ∈ S_p, Σ a finite set of places and M a smooth 𝒪[U_Σ]-module finite over 𝒪: S_λ(U, M) is the space of f : G(F⁺)\G(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) → 𝒱_λ ⊗ M with u · f(gu) = f(g). Lemma 1.24: for U sufficiently small and M 𝒪-flat, S_λ(U, M) ⊗ 𝒪/ϖ^c ≅ S_λ(U, M/ϖ^c). Lemma 1.25: S_λ(U, M) ⊗_{𝒪,ι} ℂ ≅ ⊕_σ m(σ)Hom_U((M ⊗ ℂ)^∨, σ^∞), Hecke-equivariantly away from Σ ∪ S_p, over σ with σ_v the dual of the algebraic representation of weight λ_{ι^{−1}τ} at infinity.
items.note: AF.5 identifies algebraic modular forms on compact-at-infinity groups with functions on finite adelic double cosets valued in an algebraic representation.

items.name: Hecke operators, Iwahori level and ordinary parts on definite unitary groups
items.statement: At split v = ww^c ∉ Σ ∪ S_p with U_v = ι_w^{−1}GL_n(𝒪_{F_w}), the unramified operators T^j_w = [ι_w^{−1}(GL_n(𝒪) diag(ϖ_w1_j, 1_{n−j}) GL_n(𝒪)) × U^v]; Iwahori subgroups Iw_w; Iw_ṽ(b, c) (upper-triangular mod ϖ^c, unipotent mod ϖ^b) at v ∈ S_p with Geraghty's renormalised U^j_{ṽ,λ}; principal congruence subgroups K_ṽ(1). With U_v = ι_ṽ^{−1}Iw_ṽ(b, c) at p there is a canonical decomposition S_λ(U, M) = S^{ord}_λ(U, M) ⊕ S^{n-ord}_λ(U, M), S^{ord} the largest summand on which every U^j_{ṽ,λ} is invertible (independent of the choice of uniformiser).
items.note: Geraghty 2019 §2.3 and Definitions 2.8, 2.13. Definite unitary Hecke algebras at Iwahori and ordinary level are in the Part II proposed by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: an analytic continuation lemma for rigid spaces
items.statement: Let α : 𝒳 → 𝒢 be a closed immersion and β : 𝒴 → 𝒢 a morphism of E-rigid spaces, and x ∈ 𝒴 with β(x) ∈ 𝒳. If β^{−1}(𝒳) contains an affinoid open neighbourhood of x, then β(𝒞) ⊂ 𝒳 for every irreducible component 𝒞 of 𝒴 containing x.
items.note: Uses Conrad's theory of irreducible components of rigid spaces (Lemma 2.2.3).

items.name: Families of (φ, Γ)-modules over rigid spaces and global triangulation
items.statement: For an E-rigid space X and v ∈ S_p: the relative Robba ring ℛ_{X,F_ṽ}; the functor D†_rig of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao (Theorem 2.2.17) sending a family of G_{F_ṽ}-representations to a family of (φ, Γ_{F_ṽ})-modules, locally finite free over ℛ_{X,F_ṽ}; the rank-one modules ℛ_{A,F_ṽ}(δ) for continuous δ : F_ṽ^× → A^× (KPX Construction 6.2.4); the (φ, γ)-cohomology H*_{φ,γ}; and KPX's global triangulation over a proper birational modification of the Zariski closure of trianguline points (KPX Theorem 6.3.9, Corollary 6.3.10).
items.note: PG.7 constructs the Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao relative Robba category with its relative Herr complexes and the source-qualified triangulation inputs.

items.name: Triangulations, trianguline parameters, and the character spaces 𝒯_v, 𝒯_v^{reg}, 𝒲_v
items.statement: For ρ_v : G_{F_ṽ} → GL_n(E) and δ_v = (δ_{v,1}, …, δ_{v,n}) : (F_ṽ^×)^n → E^×, a triangulation of parameter δ_v is an increasing filtration of D†_rig(ρ_v) by direct summand (φ, Γ)-stable ℛ-submodules with graded pieces ℛ(δ_{v,1}), …, ℛ(δ_{v,n}); ρ_v is trianguline of parameter δ_v if one exists. δ_v is ordinary if each δ_{v,i}(ϖ_ṽ) ∈ 𝒪^× (then triangulations are Galois-stable filtrations with graded pieces δ_{v,i} ∘ Art^{−1}), and regular if δ_{v,i}/δ_{v,j} ≠ x^{a} for all i < j and a ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^{Hom(F_ṽ,E)}. 𝒯_v = Hom((F_ṽ^×)^n, 𝔾_m) (smooth), 𝒯_v^{reg} ⊂ 𝒯_v the Zariski open regular locus, 𝒲_v = Hom((𝒪^×)^n, 𝔾_m) and r_v : 𝒯_v → 𝒲_v restriction. Definition 2.5: the labelled weights wt_τ(δ) are defined by δ′(x) = −Σ_τ wt_τ(δ)τ(x). Artinian versions over A ∈ 𝒞′_E.

items.name: Lemma 2.4: uniqueness of triangulations of regular parameter
items.statement: For δ_v ∈ 𝒯_v^{reg}(E), ρ_v admits at most one triangulation of parameter δ_v, and if it exists ρ_v is strictly trianguline of parameter δ_v (KPX Definition 6.3.1).
items.note: KPX Proposition 6.2.8 and dévissage.

items.name: Proposition 2.6: the trianguline deformation functor
items.statement: For δ_v ∈ 𝒯_v^{reg}(E) and a triangulation F_v, the functor D_{ρ_v,F_v,δ_v} on 𝒞′_E of triples (lift ρ′_v, lift δ′_v, triangulation F′_v of parameter δ′_v lifting F_v) up to (1 + M_n(m_A))-conjugacy maps to D_{ρ_v} relatively representably and injectively on A-points; if ρ_v is absolutely irreducible both are pro-representable and R_{ρ_v} → R_{ρ_v,F_v,δ_v} is surjective. Hence H¹_{tri,δ_v}(F_ṽ, ad ρ_v) ⊂ H¹(F_ṽ, ad ρ_v) depends only on δ_v, with a linear map to T_{r_v(δ_v)}𝒲_v.
items.note: Bellaïche–Chenevier Propositions 2.3.6, 2.3.9 for F_ṽ = ℚ_p; Nakamura 2013 (B-pairs) in general.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: trianguline deformations of fixed weight are de Rham
items.statement: If ρ_v is de Rham and trianguline of parameter δ_v ∈ 𝒯_v^{reg}(E) with wt_τ(δ_{v,1}) < ⋯ < wt_τ(δ_{v,n}) for each τ (these are the labelled Hodge–Tate weights), then ker(H¹_{tri,δ_v}(F_ṽ, ad ρ) → T_{r_v(δ_v)}𝒲_v) maps into H¹_g(F_ṽ, ad ρ) = ker(H¹(F_ṽ, ad ρ) → H¹(F_ṽ, ad ρ ⊗ B_dR)). A triangulation with this weight condition is called non-critical.
items.locator: §2.3.1, Lemma 2.7 and the definition after it, pp. 30–31
items.note: Bellaïche–Chenevier Proposition 2.3.4, Hellmann–Schraen Proposition 2.6 (over Artinian coefficients).

items.name: Lemma 2.8 and Definition 2.9: a numerical criterion for non-critical triangulations
items.statement: Let ρ_v : G_{F_ṽ} → GL_n(Q̄_p) be de Rham with (1) an increasing filtration of WD(ρ_v) with graded characters χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n}, (2) distinct τ-Hodge–Tate weights k_{τ,1} < ⋯ < k_{τ,n}, and (3) v_p(χ_{v,1}(p)) < k_{τ,2} + Σ_{τ′≠τ}k_{τ′,1} and v_p((χ_{v,1}⋯χ_{v,i})(p)) < k_{τ,i+1} + Σ_{τ′≠τ}k_{τ′,i} + Σ_{τ′}Σ_{j<i}k_{τ′,j} (2 ≤ i ≤ n − 1). Then ρ_v is trianguline of parameter δ_{v,i}(x) = (χ_{v,i} ∘ Art(x))∏_τ τ(x)^{−k_{τ,i}}, and this triangulation is non-critical. Definition 2.9: δ_v is numerically non-critical if its labelled weights increase and v_p((δ_{v,1}⋯δ_{v,i})(p)) < wt_τ(δ_{v,i+1}) − wt_τ(δ_{v,i}) for all τ and i; for Hodge–Tate regular de Rham ρ_v with a Weil–Deligne filtration, a numerically non-critical δ_v yields a non-critical triangulation.
items.note: Generalises Hellmann–Schraen Lemma 2.9 (crystalline case). Proof: Breuil–Schneider Proposition 4.1 and Berger's equivalence between filtered (φ, N, G)-modules and (φ, Γ)-modules, with weak admissibility (t_N ≥ t_H).

items.name: Example 2.10: triangulations of two-dimensional de Rham representations of G_{ℚ_p}
items.statement: Let ρ : G_{ℚ_p} → GL_2(Q̄_p) be de Rham with Hodge–Tate weights k_1 < k_2 and WD(ρ)^{ss} = χ_1 ⊕ χ_2, χ_1 ≠ χ_2. (1) If ρ is not potentially crystalline (χ_1 = χ_2|·|), it has a unique triangulation, non-critical, of parameter (x^{−k_1}χ_1 ∘ Art, x^{−k_2}χ_2 ∘ Art). (2) If ρ is potentially crystalline and irreducible, or reducible indecomposable, it has two triangulations, both non-critical, of parameters (x^{−k_1}χ_1, x^{−k_2}χ_2) and (x^{−k_1}χ_2, x^{−k_2}χ_1). (3) If ρ ≅ ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2 (ψ_i of weight k_i), it has a non-critical triangulation (x^{−k_1}χ_1, x^{−k_2}χ_2) and a critical one (x^{−k_2}χ_2, x^{−k_1}χ_1).
items.note: Colmez 2008; justified for p = 2 too by Berger 2008; Bergdall Example 3.7.

items.name: Proposition 2.15: the trianguline locus near an absolutely irreducible point
items.statement: Let ρ_v be absolutely irreducible and trianguline of parameter δ_v ∈ 𝒯_v^{reg}(E), z = (ρ_v, δ_v) ∈ 𝒳^{v-irr}_{ps,v} × 𝒯_v^{reg}. (1) There is an affinoid neighbourhood 𝒰_v of z carrying a universal representation, and the set 𝒱_v of points (ρ′_v, δ′_v) with ρ′_v trianguline of parameter δ′_v is Zariski open in its Zariski closure 𝒵_v. (2) The Zariski tangent space of 𝒵_v at z lies in H¹_{tri,δ_v}(F_ṽ, ad ρ_v).
items.note: Proof: KPX Corollary 6.3.10 (proper birational Z′ → 𝒵_v with a global triangulation off a closed set), Köpf's relative analytification and EGA I 3.9.8 for injectivity of completed local rings.

items.name: Remark 2.16: KPX's global triangulation holds for the standard notion of Zariski density
items.statement: KPX Definition 6.3.2 requires density in each member of an admissible affinoid cover; Theorem 6.3.9 of loc. cit. nevertheless holds when X_alg is Zariski dense in the usual sense: for X normal and connected, the points of X_alg in the Zariski open locus U′ where H^i_{φ,γ}(M^∨(δ)) and H^i_{φ,γ}(M^∨(δ)/t_σ) are locally free and the relevant fibre maps are non-zero form a set dense in every affinoid.
items.note: An argument explained to the authors by E. Hellmann, prompted by a referee.

items.name: Polarized Galois representations to 𝒢_n and their deformation functor
items.statement: 𝒢_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {±1} (Clozel–Harris–Taylor §2.1) with multiplier ν_{𝒢_n}; for ρ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(E) with ν ∘ ρ = ϵ^{1−n}δ^n_{F/F⁺}, ad ρ is the adjoint action on Lie GL_n and D_ρ is the functor of ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(E))-conjugacy classes of lifts with the same multiplier; restriction ρ|_Δ to Δ ⊂ G_{F,S} is the projection to GL_n.
items.note: Polarized deformation functors are GlobalGaloisDeformations G7.

items.name: Proposition 2.11: a bound on global trianguline deformations
items.statement: Let δ ∈ 𝒯^{reg}(E) with ρ_v = ρ|_{G_{F_ṽ}} trianguline of parameter δ_v (v ∈ S_p), D_{ρ,F,δ} = D_ρ ×_{∏D_{ρ_v}} ∏D_{ρ_v,F_v,δ_v} and H¹_{tri,δ}(F_S/F⁺, ad ρ) = D_{ρ,F,δ}(E[ϵ]). If (1) each ρ_v is de Rham, (2) WD(ρ|_{G_{F_ṽ}}) is generic (Allen Definition 1.1.2) for v ∈ S, (3) each triangulation is non-critical and (4) H¹_f(F⁺, ad ρ) = 0, then dim_E H¹_{tri,δ}(F_S/F⁺, ad ρ) ≤ dim_E 𝒲.
items.note: Genericity gives H¹_f = H¹_g at p and H¹_f = H¹ away from p (Allen Remark 1.2.9).

items.name: Conjugate self-dual pseudocharacters and their pseudodeformation rings
items.statement: Continuous pseudocharacters in Chenevier's sense (determinants) τ̄ : G_{F,S} → k of dimension n, conjugate self-dual (τ̄ ∘ c = τ̄^∨ ⊗ ϵ^{1−n}), the universal ring R_ps of conjugate self-dual pseudodeformations of τ̄ over 𝒞_𝒪 (Newton–Thorne 2020 §2.19) and R_{ps,v} for τ̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}; closed points of the rigid generic fibre correspond to semisimple conjugate self-dual representations.
items.note: Determinants are IHG.0, reconstruction of representations from determinants IHG.1, and pseudorepresentation deformation functors R04.1.

items.name: The rigid spaces 𝒳_ps, 𝒳_{ps,v} and their absolutely irreducible loci
items.statement: 𝒳_ps and 𝒳_{ps,v} are the rigid generic fibres of R_ps and R_{ps,v}, with 𝒳_ps → 𝒳_{ps,p} = ∏_{v∈S_p}𝒳_{ps,v}; 𝒳^{v-irr}_{ps,v} is the Zariski open locus where the universal pseudocharacter is absolutely irreducible, carrying an Azumaya algebra 𝒜 and ρ^u_v : G_{F_ṽ} → 𝒜^× with trace the universal pseudocharacter (Chenevier §4.2); 𝒳^{p-irr}_{ps} is the preimage of ∏𝒳^{v-irr}_{ps,v}. Lemma 2.13: at an absolutely irreducible point z, 𝒜 splits on an affinoid neighbourhood, 𝒜|_𝒰 ≅ M_n(𝒪_𝒰) (the stalk is Henselian).

items.name: Lemma 2.12: polarized lifts versus conjugate self-dual traces
items.statement: Let ρ : G_{F,S} → GL_n(E) be absolutely irreducible with ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗ ϵ^{1−n}, extended to ρ_1 : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(E) with ν ∘ ρ_1 = ϵ^{1−n}δ^a (a ∈ {0, 1} determined by ρ). For A ∈ 𝒞_E, conjugacy classes of lifts ρ′ of ρ with tr ρ′ ∘ c = tr(ρ′)^∨ ⊗ ϵ^{1−n} correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of lifts ρ′_1 of ρ_1 with ν ∘ ρ′_1 = ϵ^{1−n}δ^a.
items.note: Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemmas 2.1.1, 2.1.4, 2.1.8 and Chenevier Example 3.4.

items.name: Lemma 2.14: tangent spaces of pseudocharacter spaces
items.statement: (1) At z ∈ 𝒳^{p-irr}_{ps,p}(E) given by absolutely irreducible (ρ_v)_{v∈S_p}, T_z𝒳^{p-irr}_{ps,p} ≅ ⊕_{v∈S_p}H¹(F_ṽ, ad ρ_v). (2) At z ∈ 𝒳^{p-irr}_{ps}(E) given by ρ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(E) with each ρ|_{G_{F_ṽ}} absolutely irreducible, T_z𝒳^{p-irr}_{ps} ≅ H¹(G_{F⁺,S}, ad ρ), compatibly with restriction.
items.note: Chenevier §4.1 and Lemma 2.12.

items.name: Tame level, Hecke algebras, weight and character spaces, and accessible refinements
items.statement: U_n = ∏U_{n,v} ⊂ G_n(𝔸^∞_{F⁺}) with U_{n,v} hyperspecial for v ∉ S; 𝕋^S_n = 𝒪[T^1_w, …, T^n_w, (T^n_w)^{−1}] at split v = ww^c ∉ S; 𝒲_n = Hom(∏_{v∈S_p}T_n(𝒪_{F_ṽ}), 𝔾_m), 𝒯_n = Hom(∏_{v∈S_p}T_n(F_ṽ), 𝔾_m), r : 𝒯_n → 𝒲_n. For π with π^{U_n} ≠ 0, ψ_π : 𝕋^S_n → Q̄_p is its Hecke eigensystem and an accessible refinement is χ = (χ_v)_{v∈S_p} with χ_v a character of T_n(F_ṽ) occurring in the normalised Jacquet module ι^{−1}r_{N_n}(π_v) (equivalently π_v ↪ i^{GL_n}_{B_n}ιχ_v).

items.name: Lemma 2.18: accessible refinements give Weil–Deligne filtrations
items.statement: If χ is an accessible refinement of π, then for each v ∈ S_p, rec^T_{F_ṽ}(ι^{−1}π_v) has an increasing filtration by sub-Weil–Deligne representations with graded pieces χ_{v,1}|·|^{(1−n)/2} ∘ Art, …, χ_{v,n}|·|^{(1−n)/2} ∘ Art.
items.note: Langlands classification and Zelevinsky Theorem 1.2 (Jacquet modules of induced Steinbergs).

items.name: The character ν(π, χ), the twist j_n and numerically non-critical refinements
items.statement: (2.18.1) ν(π, χ) = κ(π) · (χ_vι^{−1}δ_{B_n}^{−1/2})_{v∈S_p} ∈ 𝒯_n(Q̄_p), κ(π) the B_n-dominant algebraic character of highest weight of ι^{−1}π_∞; if κ(π)_v = (κ_{τ,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ κ_{τ,n}) the labelled Hodge–Tate weights of r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_ṽ}} are −κ_{τ,1} < −κ_{τ,2} + 1 < ⋯ < −κ_{τ,n} + n − 1. j_n(ν)_v = ν_v · (1, ϵ^{−1} ∘ Art, …, ϵ^{1−n} ∘ Art); j_n(ν(π, χ)) is the parameter δ of Lemma 2.8 for χ|·|^{(1−n)/2}, and χ is numerically non-critical (resp. ordinary) if δ is. Remark 2.21: this is Emerton's non-critical slope (Definition 4.4.3) for κ(π)_vχ_vδ_{B_n}^{1/2}, the renormalisation relative to Bellaïche–Chenevier coming from the unnormalised Jacquet module.

items.name: Emerton's eigenvariety ℰ_n for the definite unitary group
items.statement: S̃(U^p_n, 𝒪) = lim_s lim_{U_p} S(U^p_nU_p, 𝒪/ϖ^s), S̃(U^p_n, E) = S̃(U^p_n, 𝒪) ⊗ E (an admissible Banach representation of G_n(F⁺_p)) with locally V_λ^∨-algebraic vectors lim S_λ(U^p_nU_p, 𝒪) ⊗ V_λ^∨ (Emerton 2006b Corollary 2.2.25); Emerton's locally analytic Jacquet functor J_{B_n} applied to the locally analytic vectors gives, by duality, a coherent sheaf ℳ_n on 𝒯_n with 𝕋^S_n-action; 𝒜_n ⊂ End(ℳ_n) is generated by 𝕋^S_n and ℰ_n = Sp_{𝒯_n}𝒜_n with finite ν′, ν = ν′ twisted by δ_{B_n}^{−1}, ψ : 𝕋^S_n → 𝒪(ℰ_n). (ψ_0, ν_0) is a point iff J_{B_n}(S̃^{an})[ψ_0, ν_0δ_{B_n}] ≠ 0; classical points Z_n are those with a non-zero map to J_{B_n}(S̃^{alg})[ψ_0].
items.note: Emerton's construction is used to avoid Iwahori level at p (unlike Bellaïche–Chenevier); the pending eigenvariety Part II builds it for definite unitary groups.

items.name: Lemma 2.19 and Lemma 2.20: eigenspaces of the Jacquet module and classical points
items.statement: Lemma 2.19: Hom_T(χ, J_{B_n}(S̃^{an})[ψ]) = Hom_T(χ, J_{B_n}(S̃^{an}[ψ])) for characters ψ of 𝕋^S_n and χ of ∏T_n(F_ṽ). Lemma 2.20: with 𝒜_n the automorphic representations π with (π^∞)^{U_n^{S_p}} ≠ 0, ℛ𝒜_n the pairs (π, χ) with χ accessible, and 𝒵_n = {(ψ_π, ν(π, χ))}, ψ* × ν restricts to a bijection Z_n → 𝒵_n.
items.note: Emerton 2006a Propositions 3.4.9 and 4.3.6, Lemma 1.25.

items.name: Proposition 2.22(1), (4): geometry of ℰ_n
items.statement: ℰ_n is a reduced E-rigid space with a finite morphism ν : ℰ_n → 𝒯_n (κ : ℰ_n → 𝒲_n the induced map); it is equidimensional of dimension dim 𝒲_n and κ(𝒞) is Zariski open in 𝒲_n for every irreducible component 𝒞.
items.note: Proof via the spectral variety 𝒴_z ⊂ 𝒲_n × 𝔾_m (a Fredholm hypersurface; Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen 2017 §3.3, Lemma 3.10, Proposition 3.11, Corollaires 3.12–3.13), a good affinoid cover, and semisimplicity of the Hecke action at très classique points (BHS Corollaire 3.20; Chenevier 2005 Proposition 3.9) for reducedness.

items.name: Proposition 2.22(2), (5): density and classicality of classical points
items.statement: Z_n ⊂ ℰ_n(Q̄_p) is Zariski dense and accumulates at every point of Z_n, and ψ* × ν restricts to a bijection Z_n → 𝒵_n; a point z with δ = j_n(ν(z)) = δ_{alg}δ_{sm} (δ_{alg} strictly dominant algebraic, δ_{sm} smooth) numerically non-critical lies in Z_n.
items.note: Emerton's classicality criterion (2006a Theorem 4.4.5); accumulation as in BHS Théorème 3.19 and Taïbi Theorem 2.1.1.

items.name: Proposition 2.22(3), (6): the Hecke algebra generates and is bounded
items.statement: For every affinoid open 𝒱 ⊂ 𝒯_n, 𝕋^S_n ⊗ 𝒪(𝒱) → 𝒪(ν^{−1}𝒱) is surjective, and ψ takes values in the bounded functions 𝒪(ℰ_n)^{≤1}. A tuple with properties (1)–(3) is unique (as in Bellaïche–Chenevier Proposition 7.2.8).

items.name: The Galois pseudocharacter over ℰ_n and the closed immersion i_n
items.statement: There is a conjugate self-dual pseudocharacter T_n : G_{F,S} → 𝒪(ℰ_n) with T_{n,z} = tr r_{π,ι} at z ∈ Z_n given by (π, χ) (Bellaïche–Chenevier Proposition 7.5.4, Chenevier 2004 Proposition 7.1.1, Chenevier 2014 Example 2.32); ℰ_n = ⊔ℰ_n(τ̄_n) over residual pseudocharacters (Chenevier Theorem 3.17); λ : ℰ_n(τ̄_n) → 𝒳_{ps,n} and i_n = λ × (j_n ∘ ν) : ℰ_n(τ̄_n) → 𝒳_{ps,n} × 𝒯_n is a closed immersion.

items.name: Lemma 2.26: the ordinary locus of ℰ_n (Hida theory)
items.statement: The Zariski closure ℰ_n(τ̄_n)^{ord} of the classical points with ordinary refinements is a union of connected components of ℰ_n(τ̄_n) finite over 𝒲_n; every classical point in it has an ordinary refinement, and its points with dominant locally algebraic image in 𝒲_n are classical.
items.note: Identified with the generic fibre of Geraghty's Hida–Hecke algebra; unitary characters (Sorensen Corollary 6.4) and Hida classicality (Geraghty Lemma 2.25).

items.name: Lemma 2.30: classicality of locally algebraic points with non-critical triangulations
items.statement: Let z ∈ ℰ_n(τ̄_n)(Q̄_p) with i_n(z) = (tr r_z, δ) ∈ 𝒳^{p-irr}_{ps,n} × 𝒯_n^{reg}, δ = j_n(ν(z)) = δ_{alg}δ_{sm} with δ_{alg} algebraic and δ_{sm} smooth, and suppose every triangulation of r_z|_{G_{F_ṽ}} (v ∈ S_p) is non-critical. Then z ∈ Z_n and δ_{alg} is strictly dominant.
items.note: Proof: KPX families near z give that r_z is trianguline of parameter δ and δ_{alg} strictly dominant (Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen 2017 Lemme 2.11, published version); failure of classicality would give a companion point with non-dominant weight (BHS Proposition 3.28, Chenevier 2011 Proposition 4.2), excluded by the same lemma.

items.name: Orlik–Strauch functors and Breuil's adjunction for completed cohomology
items.statement: For η = ν(z)δ_{B_n} = η_{alg}η_{sm}, the locally analytic representation ℱ^{G_n}_{B_n}(ηδ_{B_n}^{−1}) = ℱ^{G_n}_{B_n}((U(𝔤_n) ⊗_{U(𝔟_n)} η_{alg}^{−1})^∨, η_{sm}δ_{B_n}^{−1}) (Orlik–Strauch; Breuil 2015 Theorem 2.2) has locally algebraic quotient V(η_{alg}) ⊗ Ind η_{sm}δ_{B_n}^{−1} and Jordan–Hölder factors ℱ^{G_n}_{P_n}(M_{w·η_{alg}}, π); Breuil's adjunction (2015 Theorem 4.3) identifies Hom_T(η, J_{B_n}(Π)) with Hom_G(ℱ^{G_n}_{B_n}(ηδ^{−1}), Π) for Π = S̃^{an}[ψ*(z)], and a non-zero map from a factor with w ≠ 1 produces a companion point (Breuil 2016 Corollary 3.4).
items.note: The Orlik–Strauch functor and adjunction are part of the pending eigenvariety Part II (PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19).

items.name: Symmetric power maps between pseudocharacter and character spaces
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and a conjugate self-dual 2-dimensional τ̄_2, τ̄_n = Sym^{n−1}τ̄_2; σ_{n,g} : 𝒳_{ps,2} → 𝒳_{ps,n} takes symmetric powers of pseudocharacters, σ_{n,p} : 𝒯_2 → 𝒯_n sends ((δ_{v,1}, δ_{v,2}))_v to ((δ_{v,1}^{n−1}, δ_{v,1}^{n−2}δ_{v,2}, …, δ_{v,2}^{n−1}))_v, and σ_n = σ_{n,g} × σ_{n,p}, giving the diagram ℰ_2(τ̄_2) → 𝒳_{ps,n} × 𝒯_n ← ℰ_n(τ̄_n) via σ_n ∘ i_2 and i_n.

items.name: Definition 2.23: n-regular refinements
items.statement: An accessible refinement χ of an automorphic representation π of G_2(𝔸_{F⁺}) is n-regular if for each v ∈ S_p, χ_v = χ_{v,1} ⊗ χ_{v,2} satisfies (χ_{v,1}/χ_{v,2})^i ≠ 1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1.

items.name: Theorem 2.24: analytic continuation of symmetric power functoriality (non-critical case)
items.statement: Let (π_2, χ_2) ∈ ℛ𝒜_2 with tr r̄_{π_2,ι} = τ̄_2 and z_2 = γ_2(π_2, χ_2). Suppose (1) χ_2 is numerically non-critical and n-regular; (2) there is (π_n, χ_n) ∈ ℛ𝒜_n with (σ_n ∘ i_2)(z_2) = i_n(z_n), z_n = γ_n(π_n, χ_n); (3) for each v ∈ S_p the Zariski closure of r_{π_2,ι}(G_{F_ṽ}) contains SL_2. Then every irreducible component 𝒞 of ℰ_2(τ̄_2)_{ℂ_p} through z_2 satisfies (σ_n ∘ i_2)(𝒞) ⊂ i_n(ℰ_n(τ̄_n)_{ℂ_p}).
items.note: Proof: Lemma 2.2; r_{π_n} is trianguline of the regular non-critical parameter σ_{n,p}(δ_2); Propositions 2.11 and 2.15 with H¹_f(F⁺, ad r_{π_n,ι}) = 0 (Newton–Thorne 2020) bound the tangent space of the trianguline locus 𝒵 by dim 𝒲_n, so ℰ_n(τ̄_n) is smooth at z_n and locally equal to 𝒵. Remark 2.25: (3) keeps all symmetric powers locally irreducible.

items.name: Theorem 2.27: analytic continuation of symmetric power functoriality (ordinary case)
items.statement: Let (π_2, χ_2), z_2 be as in Theorem 2.24 and suppose (1) χ_2 is ordinary; (2) there is (π_n, χ_n) ∈ ℛ𝒜_n with (σ_n ∘ i_2)(z_2) = i_n(z_n); (3) the Zariski closure of r_{π_2,ι}(G_F) contains SL_2. Then every irreducible component 𝒞 of ℰ_2(τ̄_2)_{ℂ_p} through z_2 satisfies (σ_n ∘ i_2)(𝒞) ⊂ i_n(ℰ_n(τ̄_n)_{ℂ_p}).
items.note: Proof: the closed subspace 𝒵^{ord} of the flag variety FL_p(𝒪^n_𝒰) of G_{F_ṽ}-stable flags with graded characters δ_{z,v,i}, the ordinary analogue of Lemma 2.7 (Geraghty Lemma 3.9) and Newton–Thorne 2020.

items.name: Corollary 2.28: symmetric power automorphy along an irreducible component
items.statement: Let (π_2, χ_2), (π′_2, χ′_2) ∈ ℛ𝒜_2 with points z_2, z′_2 ∈ ℰ_2(Q̄_p). Suppose either (1) χ_2 is numerically non-critical and n-regular, (2) every triangulation of r_{π′_2,ι}|_{G_{F_ṽ}} is non-critical (v ∈ S_p) and χ′_2 is n-regular, (3) the Zariski closures of r_{π_2,ι}(G_{F_ṽ}) and r_{π′_2,ι}(G_{F_ṽ}) contain SL_2, (4) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_2,ι} ≅ r_{π_n,ι} for an automorphic π_n of G_n(𝔸_{F⁺}) and (5) z_2, z′_2 lie on a common irreducible component of ℰ_{2,ℂ_p}; or (1ord) χ_2 ordinary, (2ord) the Zariski closure of r_{π_2,ι}(G_F) contains SL_2, (3ord) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_2,ι} ≅ r_{π_n,ι} and (4ord) a common irreducible component. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_2,ι} ≅ r_{π′_n,ι} for an automorphic representation π′_n of G_n(𝔸_{F⁺}).
items.note: The refinement χ_n = (χ_{2,v,1}^{n−1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ χ_{2,v,2}^{n−1}) is accessible (Zelevinsky Theorem 9.7, Rodier §4.4); classicality at z′_n from Lemma 2.26 (ordinary) or Lemmas 2.29–2.30.

items.name: Lemma 2.29: non-criticality passes to symmetric powers
items.statement: Let ρ_v : G_{F_ṽ} → GL_2(Q̄_p) be continuous, regular and de Rham, with WD(ρ_v) having distinct Jordan–Hölder characters χ_1, χ_2 with (χ_1/χ_2)^i ≠ 1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, and suppose every triangulation of ρ_v is non-critical. Then every triangulation of Sym^{n−1}ρ_v is non-critical.
items.note: Proof with the filtered (φ, N, Gal(L/K))-module: if N ≠ 0 the triangulation is unique; if N = 0, lines l_τ = ⟨e_1 + a_τe_2⟩ and a Vandermonde determinant (Chenevier 2011 Example 3.26).

items.name: The vanishing of adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer groups (Newton–Thorne 2020)
items.statement: For the automorphic representations π_n of G_n used here (with r_{π_n,ι} irreducible and the base change cuspidal), H¹_f(F⁺, ad r_{π_n,ι}) = 0.
items.locator: §2.18.1, proof of Theorem 2.24, p. 47; proof of Theorem 2.27, p. 49
items.note: Imported from Newton–Thorne, Adjoint Selmer groups of automorphic Galois representations of unitary type (JEMS). This is the input that turns the eigenvariety into a smooth space near z_n, following Kisin (GL_2) and Bellaïche–Chenevier.

items.name: The Coleman–Mazur eigencurve of tame level N
items.statement: For N ≥ 1 prime to p: 𝒯_0 = Hom(ℚ_p^×/ℤ_p^× × ℚ_p^×, 𝔾_m), 𝒲_0 = Hom(ℤ_p^×, 𝔾_m), r_0(χ_{0,1} ⊗ χ_{0,2}) = χ_{0,2}^{−1}|_{ℤ_p^×}, 𝕋^{pN}_0 = 𝒪[T_l, S_l]_{l∤pN}, U_1(N). The eigencurve (ℰ_0, ψ_0, ν_0, Z_0) is a reduced E-rigid space with finite ν_0 : ℰ_0 → 𝒯_0, bounded ψ_0 and a self-accumulating Zariski dense Z_0, equidimensional of dimension 1 with κ(𝒞) Zariski open, Z_0 in bijection with pairs (π_0, χ_0) (π_0 cuspidal of weight k ≥ 2 with (π_0^∞)^{U_1(N)^p} ≠ 0, χ_0 accessible with χ_{0,1} unramified) via ν_0(π_0, χ_0)(diag(t_1, t_2)) = t_2^{2−k}χ_{0,1}(t_1)χ_{0,2}(t_2)|t_1/t_2|^{−1/2} (2.31.1), and 𝕋 ⊗ 𝒪(𝒱) → 𝒪(ν_0^{−1}𝒱) surjective; it carries a pseudocharacter t with t_z = tr r_{π_0,ι}. The slope s(z) = v_p(χ(diag(p, 1))) equals v_p(ι^{−1}a_p(f)) at classical points; (π_0, χ_0) is numerically non-critical iff s < k − 1 and ordinary iff s = 0; Coleman's classicality: a point of weight t ↦ t^{k−2} (on a finite-index subgroup) and slope s < k − 1 is classical.
items.note: PadicFamilies L2 builds the eigencurve with its classicality theorem in the small-slope range, via L2a's group-independent construction, whose normative sources are Buzzard's Eigenvarieties and Coleman–Mazur. Uniqueness is Bellaïche–Chenevier Proposition 7.2.8; normalisations as in Diamond–Im §11.

items.name: The twin map and Lemma 2.32
items.statement: For z ∈ Z_0^{pc} (π_{0,p} not a twist of Steinberg) with pair (π_0, χ_{0,1} ⊗ χ_{0,2}), let ψ be the finite-order character unramified outside p with ψ|_{ℤ_p^×} = χ_{0,2}^{−1}|_{ℤ_p^×}; the twin τ(z) ∈ Z_0^{pc} is the point of (π_0 ⊗ ιψ, χ_{0,2}ψ ⊗ χ_{0,1}ψ), τ² = 1 (for π_{0,p} unramified it is the Gouvêa–Mazur companion point of the infinite fern). Lemma 2.32: the slopes satisfy s + s′ = k − 1 and v_p(κ(z)(1 + q) − 1) = v_p(κ(z′)(1 + q) − 1), q = p for p odd and q = 4 for p = 2.

items.name: Theorem 2.33: analytic continuation of symmetric power automorphy on the eigencurve
items.statement: Let (π_0, χ_0), (π′_0, χ′_0) ∈ ℛ𝒜_0, n ≥ 2, with points z_0, z′_0 ∈ Z_0 on a common irreducible component of ℰ_{0,ℂ_p}. Suppose either (1) χ_0 is numerically non-critical and n-regular, (2) χ′_0 is n-regular, (3) the Zariski closures of r_{π_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) and r_{π′_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) contain SL_2 and (4) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic; or (1ord) χ_0 is ordinary, (2ord) π_0, π′_0 are not CM and (3ord) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_0,ι} is automorphic.
items.note: Proof: an abelian CM field F′ (primes dividing Np split, [F′⁺ : ℚ] even, F′/F′⁺ unramified), a character ψ from Lemma 2.34, a soluble CM F ⊃ F′, a base-change morphism b : 𝒳_{0,ps} × 𝒯̃ → 𝒳_{2,ps} × 𝒯_2, descent to G_2 (Labesse Théorème 5.4), Corollary 2.28 and soluble descent for GL_n; Example 2.10 converts (3) into non-criticality of all triangulations.

items.name: Lemma 2.34: trivialising a family of characters over a CM field
items.statement: Let F be CM with every p-adic place of F⁺ split, S̃_p a set of p-adic places with S̃_p ⊔ S̃_p^c all of them, W a connected E-rigid space and χ : G_ℚ → 𝒪(W)^× continuous and unramified almost everywhere. Then there are a finite étale η : W̃ → W and a continuous ψ : G_F → 𝒪(W̃)^×, unramified almost everywhere and at each ṽ ∈ S̃_p, with ψψ^c = η*(χ)|_{G_F}.
items.note: Proof: Chevalley's theorem on units, finite étaleness of restriction of character spaces (cf. Buzzard 2004 §2), and Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor Lemma A.2.5.

items.name: Lemma 2.35: the locus where the hypotheses of Theorem 2.33 fail is Zariski closed
items.statement: Fix n ≥ 1. The set Z ⊂ ℰ_0 of points x with t_x absolutely reducible, or t_x = tr ρ_x with ρ_x absolutely irreducible whose image has Zariski closure not containing SL_2, or t_x|_{G_{ℚ_l}} = χ_1 + χ_2 with (χ_1/χ_2)^i = 1 for some l | N and 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, is Zariski closed.
items.note: Chenevier §4.2 for reducibility; the Zariski closure contains SL_2 iff Sym^6ρ_x is irreducible (finite subgroups of PGL_2 and torus normalisers).

items.name: Theorem 3.2(1)–(2): Buzzard–Kilford's description of the 2-adic eigencurve near the boundary
items.statement: Take p = 2, N = 1 (ℰ_0 is then supported on the component 𝒲_0⁺ where χ(−1) = 1) and w = χ^u(5) − 1 ∈ 𝒪(𝒲_0). (1) w identifies 𝒲_0⁺ with the open unit disc {|w| < 1}. (2) Over 𝒲_0(b) = {|8| < |w| < 1}, ℰ_0(b) = κ^{−1}(𝒲_0(b)) = ⊔_{i≥1}X_i is a countable disjoint union of admissible opens with each κ|_{X_i} : X_i → 𝒲_0(b) an isomorphism.
items.note: Buzzard–Kilford 2005, transferred to the cuspidal eigencurve since the ordinary locus of the full eigencurve is the Eisenstein family (Pilloni §6; Buzzard–Calegari arXiv Lemma 7.4). A theorem about PadicFamilies' eigencurve that no layer plans.

items.name: Theorem 3.2(3): slopes on the Buzzard–Kilford annuli
items.statement: For each i ≥ 1, s ∘ κ|_{X_i}^{−1} : 𝒲_0(b)(ℂ_p) → ℝ equals i · v_p ∘ w. In particular there are no newforms of level 4 and odd slope (Buzzard–Kilford, Corollary of Theorem B).

items.name: Lemma 3.3: the twin of a point on X_i
items.statement: Let z ∈ Z_0^{pc} ∩ ℰ_0(b) with z ∈ X_i and z′ = τ(z). Then z′ ∈ X_{i′} with i + i′ = (k − 1)/v_p(w(z)) (an integer).
items.note: Printed with 'z ∈ X_{i′}' (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Lemma 3.4: refinements of level-one forms at 2
items.statement: Every accessible refinement at 2 of an everywhere unramified cuspidal π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 is numerically non-critical and n-regular for every n ≥ 2.
items.note: No level-1 cusp form is 2-ordinary; if α/β were a root of unity ζ, congruences with Eisenstein series mod 5 and mod 7 force ζ into incompatible sets (argument of F. Diamond, avoiding Hatada's congruence).

items.name: Lemma 3.5(1): local reducibility is ordinarity
items.statement: For π cuspidal of weight k ≥ 2 and any prime p, r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is reducible iff π is ι-ordinary.
items.note: Thorne 2015 Theorem 2.4 and Lemma 2.3.

items.name: Lemma 3.5(2): local image containing SL_2
items.statement: If either r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_p}} is irreducible and π_p admits a 3-regular refinement, or k > 2 and r_{π,ι} is not potentially crystalline, then the Zariski closure of r_{π,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) in GL_2 contains SL_2.
items.note: Sen's theorem on Lie algebras of Hodge–Tate representations.

items.name: Lemma 3.5(3): level-one forms at 2
items.statement: If p = 2 and π is everywhere unramified, the Zariski closure of r_{π,ι}(G_{ℚ_2}) contains SL_2.
items.note: An induced local representation would force T_2-eigenvalue 0, excluded as in Lemma 3.4.

items.name: Lemma 3.6: moving within one annulus
items.statement: Let z, z′ ∈ Z_0 ∩ X_i(ℂ_p) with pairs (π, χ), (π′, χ′), χ and χ′ n-regular. If Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic, so is Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι}.
items.note: Theorem 2.33 with X_i ≅ 𝒲_0(b) irreducible, Lemma 3.5.

items.name: Lemma 3.7: a ping-pong move
items.statement: Let π be everywhere unramified of weight k ≥ 2 with a refinement χ. There is m_π ≥ 1 such that for every m ≥ m_π there is a cuspidal π′ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ), unramified outside 2, with two accessible refinements of distinct slopes, a refinement χ′ with (π, χ), (π′, χ′) on the same irreducible component of ℰ_{0,ℂ_p}, κ(z′) ∈ 𝒲_0(b), twin z″ = τ(z′) ∈ X_{2^m−1}, and such that automorphy of any one of Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι}, Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι}, Sym^{n−1}r_{π″,ι} implies all three.
items.note: Take z′ ∈ X_i with κ(z′)(5) = 5^{k′−2}, k′ = 2i + 2^{m+1} − 1, classical by Coleman since s(z′) = 2i < k′ − 1; footnote 6 explains the name.

items.name: The data of §4: π = π_2 ⊞ π_{n−2} with the auxiliary place sets T_1, T_2, T_3
items.statement: n = 2k + 1 ≥ 3 odd; π_2, π_{n−2} cuspidal conjugate self-dual on GL_2(𝔸_F), GL_{n−2}(𝔸_F) with (1) π = π_2 ⊞ π_{n−2} regular algebraic (ρ = ρ_2 ⊕ ρ_{n−2}, both tempered), (2) π ι-ordinary, (3) disjoint non-empty sets of places of F⁺ outside S with q_v odd and π unramified outside S ∪ T: T_1 inert, q_v a primitive 6th root of unity mod p, char k(v) > n, π_{2,ṽ} ≅ St_2(χ_ṽ), π_{n−2,ṽ} ≅ ⊞_{i=0}^{2k−2}χ_{ṽ,i} with χ_ṽ, χ_{ṽ,0} unramified and χ_{ṽ,i}|_{𝒪^×} = ω(ṽ) (i ≥ 1); T_2 split, q_v ≡ −1 mod p, π_{2,ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ) (n_1 = 2) and π_{n−2,ṽ} ⊇ ω(ṽ) ∘ det; T_3 split, q_v a primitive (n − 2)th root of unity mod p, π_{n−2,ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ) (n_1 = n − 2) and π_{2,ṽ} ⊇ ω(ṽ) ∘ det; and characters θ_v of C(k(v)) of order p for v ∈ T_1.

items.name: Theorem 4.1: level raising to a type on a definite unitary group
items.statement: With the data of §4, for every totally real S ∪ T-split quadratic L⁺/F⁺ and L = L⁺F there is a RACSDC automorphic representation Π of GL_n(𝔸_L) with (1) Π ι-ordinary and unramified outside S ∪ T; (2) r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}|_{G_L}; (3) for v ∈ T_{1,L}, Π_ṽ|_{r_ṽ} contains λ̃(ṽ, θ̃_v, n)|_{r_ṽ} (the conditions of Proposition 1.19); (4) for v ∈ T_{2,L} ∪ T_{3,L}, Π_ṽ|_{q_ṽ} contains λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ|_F, n).
items.note: Proof: Proposition 4.6 gives σ with τ_g in σ_T; the congruence of types (Proposition 1.15) and exactness of S^{ord}_λ(U, −) give Σ containing λ_g, and cuspidality of its base change follows from Lemma 4.5 and Proposition 1.16 via the identities (4.6.4), (4.6.5). Remark 4.2: T_2 ∪ T_3 serve to force cuspidality.

items.name: Lemma 4.3 and Remark 4.4: local components at inert places
items.statement: If v is inert in F then π_ṽ ∈ A^θ_t(GL_n(F_ṽ))⁺. Consequently, for v ∈ T_1, χ_ṽ is the non-trivial unramified quadratic character and χ_{ṽ,0} is trivial.
items.note: Bellaïche–Chenevier 2011 (the sign of r_{π,ι}) extends the parameter to ^LG.

items.name: Lemma 4.5: box sums with the same residual representation are cuspidal or of shape (n − 2, 2)
items.statement: Let π′ = π′_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ π′_r be regular algebraic with π′_i cuspidal conjugate self-dual, r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι} and π′_ṽ|_{q_ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) for v ∈ T_2 ∪ T_3. Then either r = 1 (π′ cuspidal), or after reordering r = 2, n_1 = n − 2, n_2 = 2, with the local types at T_2, T_3 distributed as for π and r̄_{π′_1|·|^{−1},ι} ≅ ρ̄_{n−2}, r̄_{π′_2|·|^{(2−n)/2},ι} ≅ ρ̄_2.

items.name: Labesse's stabilised trace formula for G
items.statement: (4.6.1) T^G_{disc}(f) = Σ_H ι(G, H)T^{M̃_H}_{disc}(f̃^H) for f = f^∞ ⊗ f_∞ with f_∞ a pseudocoefficient of discrete series, the sum over endoscopic data, ι(G, H) as in Labesse Proposition 4.11, and (4.6.2) T^{M̃_H}_{disc}(f̃^H) = Σ_L Σ_{s∈W^{M̃_H}(L)_{reg}} Σ_{π̃_L} (|det(s − 1|a_L/a_{M_H})| |W^{M_H}(L)|)^{−1} tr I_Q(π̃_L)(f̃^H) (Labesse Proposition 3.4).
items.note: ET.4 builds the stable and twisted unitary trace formulas, citing Labesse 2011 §§3–4.

items.name: Proposition 4.6: a σ with prescribed types via the trace formula
items.statement: For every S ∪ T-split totally real quadratic L⁺/F⁺ (L = L⁺F), either there is an automorphic σ of G(𝔸_{F⁺}) with base change π, σ_v^{U_v} ≠ 0 for v ∉ T and σ_T|_{U_T} ⊇ τ_g = ⊗_{T_1}τ(v, n) ⊗_{T_2∪T_3}λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n), or there is such a σ of G(𝔸_{L⁺}) with base change π_L, σ_v^{U_{L,v}} ≠ 0 for v ∉ T_L and σ_{T_L}|_{U_{L,T_L}} ⊇ τ_{g,L}.
items.note: Proof: the refined identity (4.6.3) Σ m(σ_i)σ_i(f) = ½(π̃(f̃) + (π_{n−2} ⊗ (π_2 ⊗ μ^{−1} ∘ det))~(f̃^{U_{n−2}×U_2})) (Shin Proposition 4.8, Moeglin–Waldspurger, Jacquet–Shalika, Hiraga Proposition 4.6); m(σ) = ½(∏ϵ ∏c_{τ_v} + ∏ϵ ∏d_{v,1}), and if it vanishes the quadratic base change gives m(σ) = ∏c_{τ_v}² ≠ 0.

items.name: Lemma 5.1: sums of characters with large ratios are primitive
items.statement: Let ρ̄ = χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n : Γ → GL_n(k) with χ_i/χ_j of order greater than n for i ≠ j. Then ρ̄ is primitive (not induced from a proper finite-index closed subgroup).
items.note: Primitivity is a hypothesis of the Allen–Newton–Thorne lifting theorem.

items.name: Ordinary deformation problems over the Iwasawa algebra Λ
items.statement: Λ_v = 𝒪[[(I^{ab}_{F_ṽ}(p))^n]], Λ = ⊗̂_{v∈S_p}Λ_v with universal characters ψ^i_v; for μ de Rham with μ(c_v) = −1 and χ_i with χ_iχ_i^c = μ, r̄ : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(k) extending ⊕χ_i, trivial at S_p; global deformation problems 𝒮_Σ = (F/F⁺, S ∪ Σ, S̃ ∪ Σ̃, Λ, r̄, μ, {R^Δ_v}_{S_p} ∪ {R^□_v}_{S−S_p} ∪ {R^{St}_v}_Σ) with R^Δ_v ordinary variable-weight liftings, R^□_v all liftings and R^{St}_v Steinberg liftings (Allen–Newton–Thorne §3; unipotent R^1_v and Steinberg R^{St}_v as in Thorne 2015 §§3.3.3–3.3.4); for Schur r̄ (Clozel–Harris–Taylor Definition 2.1.6) the functor is represented by R_{𝒮_Σ} ∈ 𝒞_Λ.
items.note: Polarized global deformation problems are G7; ordinary flag conditions L8; Steinberg and unipotent conditions away from p R08.2.

items.name: Theorem 5.2: finiteness of residually reducible ordinary deformation rings
items.statement: Suppose (1) p > 2n; (2) for 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n, χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has order greater than 2n (so r̄ is Schur); (3) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1; (4) Σ is non-empty. Then R_{𝒮_Σ} is a finite Λ-algebra.
items.note: Proof: pass to r_2 = the GSp_{2n}-induction of r̄ ⊗ (ψ, ϵ^{1−2n}μ^{−1}δ) (BLGGT14 §1.1), primitive and multiplicity free; potential automorphy (BLGGT14 Theorem 3.1.2, with the extra condition t(P) < 0 at Σ) gives a Steinberg-at-Σ ordinary π; Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 6.2 makes R_{𝒮′} finite over Λ_{L,2n}; pseudocharacter rings (Thorne 2015 Proposition 3.29, ANT Proposition 2.5) and Lemma 5.3 transfer finiteness.

items.name: Lemma 5.3: restriction of pseudodeformations to a finite-index subgroup is finite
items.statement: Let Γ be a topologically finitely generated profinite group, Σ ⊂ Γ closed of finite index and t̄ a pseudocharacter of Γ over k. Then Q_{t̄|_Σ} → Q_{t̄} (restriction of lifts) is a finite ring map.
items.note: Chenevier 2014 Corollary 1.14.

items.name: Corollary 5.4: ordinary lifts of every weight
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 5.2, for λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,Q̄_p)} with λ_{τc,i} = −λ_{τ,n+1−i} and [F_ṽ : ℚ_p] > n(n − 1)/2 + 1 (v ∈ S_p), there is r : G_{F⁺,S} → 𝒢_n(ℤ̄_p) lifting r̄ with r|_{G_{F,S}} ordinary of weight λ (Thorne 2015 Definition 2.5).
items.note: Thorne 2015 Propositions 3.9, 3.14; Geraghty Definition 2.24.

items.name: Corollary 5.5: a dimension bound for R_{𝒮_∅}
items.statement: Under hypotheses (1)–(3) of Theorem 5.2, with v_0 ∉ S split, q_{v_0} ≡ 1 mod p and r̄|_{G_{F_{ṽ_0}}} trivial, A = R_{𝒮_∅}/(ϖ, {tr r_{𝒮_∅}(Frob^i_{ṽ_0}) − n}_{i=1,…,n}) is a finite Λ-algebra, and dim R_{𝒮_∅}/(ϖ) ≤ n[F⁺ : ℚ] + n.
items.note: Taylor 2008 §3 (the Steinberg ring contains the unipotent Frobenius quotient).

items.name: Proposition 5.6: the reducible locus is small
items.statement: Let R_𝒮/(ϖ) → A be a surjection onto a domain with r = r_1 ⊕ r_2 over A, R ⊂ S − S_p of odd residue characteristic with n_ṽ, q_ṽ a primitive n_ṽ-th root of unity mod p, r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} = σ̄_{ṽ,1} ⊕ σ̄_{ṽ,2} as in §1.17 and Θ_ṽ of order p. If (1) p > 2n, (2) χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has order > 2n, (3) [F_ṽ : ℚ_p] > n(n − 1)/2 + 1, (4) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1, (5) for v ∈ R both r̄_1|_{G_{F_ṽ}}, r̄_2|_{G_{F_ṽ}} have non-trivial unramified subquotients and R^□_v → A factors over R(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n), then dim A ≤ n[F⁺ : ℚ] + n − d_R, d_R the ℤ_p-rank of the subgroup of Δ = Gal(L_{S_p}/F)/(c + 1) generated by the Frob_ṽ (v ∈ R).
items.note: Proof: Allen–Newton–Thorne Lemma 3.6, Thorne 2015 Corollary 3.12 and Lemma 3.36, Theorem 5.2 for the two blocks and Proposition 1.22(3).

items.name: Theorem 5.7: generic primes in large quotients
items.statement: With the global deformation problem 𝒮 = (F/F⁺, S, S̃, Λ, r̄, μ, {R^Δ_v}_{S_p} ∪ {R(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n)}_R ∪ {R^□_v}), R = R_1 ⊔ R_2, 2 ≤ n < p/2, χ_i/χ_j of order > 2n, [F_ṽ : ℚ_p] > n(n − 1)/2 + 1 and [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1: let R_𝒮 → B be a surjection with B finite over Λ/(ϖ). If (1) every irreducible component of Spec B has dimension > sup({n[F⁺ : ℚ] + n − d_{R_i}}, {n[F⁺ : ℚ] − [F_ṽ : ℚ_p]}) and (2) for every decomposition r̄ = r̄_1 ⊕ r̄_2 some R_i has both r̄_1, r̄_2 with unramified subquotients at every v ∈ R_i, then some prime p ⊂ R_𝒮 of dimension 1 and characteristic p containing ker(R_𝒮 → B) is generic (Allen–Newton–Thorne Definition 3.7: distinct, ℤ-linearly independent universal characters at p, and r_p ⊗ Frac absolutely irreducible).
items.note: Allen–Newton–Thorne Lemmas 3.8–3.9, the reducibility ideal, Thorne 2015 Lemma 1.9.

items.name: Proposition 5.8: automorphic lifts of prescribed types from residual automorphy over a soluble extension
items.statement: Let F_0 be imaginary CM with F_0/F_0⁺ unramified, S_0 ⊇ S_{0,p} (p-adic places split), ρ̄ = ⊕ρ̄_i : G_{F_0,S_0} → GL_n(k) with ρ̄_i absolutely irreducible, ρ̄_i^c ≅ ρ̄_i^∨ ⊗ ϵ^{1−n}, pairwise non-isomorphic; T_0, Σ_0 ⊂ S_0 prime-to-p split, q ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄ trivial at Σ_0; quotients R^□_v → R_v (unions of components) at T_0; ρ̄(I) of order prime to p at inert places; λ with λ_{τc,i} = −λ_{τ,n+1−i} and ordinary lifts of weight λ_ṽ at p (Geraghty Definition 3.8). If a soluble CM F/F_0 satisfies (1) p > max(n, 3), [F_v : ℚ_p] > n(n − 1)/2 + 1 and ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} trivial at v | p; (2) F(ζ_p) ⊄ F^{ker ad ρ̄}, F ⊄ F⁺(ζ_p), ρ̄_i|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} absolutely irreducible and distinct, ρ̄|_{G_F} primitive with no quotient of order p; (3) there is a RACSDC ι-ordinary π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π,ι} ≅ ρ̄|_{G_F} and an unramified Steinberg twist at a place above Σ_0; (4) places above S_0 split in F — then there is a RACSDC π_0 of GL_n(𝔸_{F_0}), unramified outside S_0, with r̄_{π_0,ι} ≅ ρ̄, ι-ordinary of weight ιλ, with points of R_v at T_0, unramified Steinberg twists at Σ_0, and inertia at inert places mapping isomorphically mod p.
items.note: Similar to Bellovin–Gee Theorem 5.2.1; proof via Kisin's potentially semistable rings, Geraghty Lemma 3.10, Bellovin–Gee Corollary 5.1.1 (Schur suffices), Lemma 5.3 and Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorems 6.1–6.2, then soluble descent.

items.name: Automorphy lifting for residually reducible representations (Allen–Newton–Thorne; Thorne 2015)
items.statement: The inputs used as stated: Allen–Newton–Thorne 2020 Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 6.1 (automorphy lifting for ι-ordinary conjugate self-dual ρ with ρ̄ a sum of characters or of pairwise distinct irreducibles, primitive, given an ι-ordinary RACSDC Π with r̄_Π ≅ ρ̄ and a twisted Steinberg local component), Theorem 6.2 (finiteness of R_𝒮 over Λ in that situation), Theorem 4.1 (J ⊂ Q for minimal primes Q of the deformation ring below a generic prime when there is no ramification outside p) and Lemmas 3.6, 3.8, 3.9; Thorne 2015's deformation theory (Propositions 3.9, 3.14, 3.26, 3.29, 4.12, 4.18, Corollary 3.12, Lemmas 1.9, 3.36).
items.note: Imported theorems; the Clozel–Thorne extraction already names Thorne 2015 as a stated input and suggests this Part II as its home.

items.name: Potential automorphy (Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor 2014, Theorem 3.1.2)
items.statement: Given a residual representation with the stated adequacy/image hypotheses, there are a Galois totally real extension L⁺/F⁺, linearly disjoint from a given field, and a regular algebraic self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{L⁺}), ι-ordinary of weight 0 and an unramified Steinberg twist at the places above p (and, with an extra condition, above Σ), realising the residual representation.
items.note: Potential automorphy assembly is ML.2 (whose selected sources include Newton–Thorne).

items.name: Automorphy lifting with residually irreducible image (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1) and auxiliary characters (Lemma A.2.5)
items.statement: BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 lifts automorphy from an automorphic residual representation with irreducible (adequate) image under potential diagonalisability; Lemma A.2.5 produces algebraic characters with prescribed ψψ^c and local conditions.
items.locator: §8, proof of Theorem 8.1, p. 110; §2, Lemma 2.34; Part II introduction, p. 65; §7, p. 99
items.note: BLGGT14 Lemma A.2.5 and the lifting theorems are in the Part II proposed by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25.

items.name: Potentially semistable and ordinary local deformation rings at p
items.statement: For an inertial type τ_ṽ and Hodge type λ_ṽ, Kisin's lifting ring R^{λ_ṽ,τ_ṽ}_ṽ is equidimensional of dimension 1 + n² + n(n − 1)[F_{0,ṽ} : ℚ_p]/2 (Kisin 2008 Theorem 3.3.4); Geraghty Lemma 3.10 gives a minimal prime whose quotient R_v is 𝒪-flat of that dimension, contains a given ordinary lift, has only ordinary Q̄_p-points of weight λ_ṽ and factors R^□_v ⊗̂ Λ_v → R^Δ_v (also for non-trivial τ_ṽ).
items.note: Kisin's potentially semistable rings are R08.3; ordinary conditions L8.

items.name: Theorem 6.1: level raising to Steinberg by Galois deformation theory
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3 odd, p > 2n and π RACSDC on GL_n(𝔸_F) with (1) π ι-ordinary; (2) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1; (3) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n with χ_i^c = χ_i^∨ϵ^{1−n} and χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} of order > 2n; (4) r̄_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_ṽ}} trivial and [F_ṽ : ℚ_p] > n(n − 1)/2 + 1 at v ∈ S_p; (5) R = R_1 ⊔ R_2 ⊂ S − S_p non-empty of odd residue characteristic with π_ṽ|_{q_ṽ} ⊇ λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n) (n_1 = 3, q_v a primitive 3rd root of unity mod p, on R_1; n_1 = n − 2, q_v a primitive (n − 2)th root, on R_2) and the splitting condition (d). For a place v_{St} above S − (S_p ∪ R) with q_{v_{St}} ≡ 1 mod p and r̄ trivial there, there is a RACSDC ι-ordinary π′ of GL_n(𝔸_F) with r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, HT_τ(r_{π′,ι}) = HT_τ(r_{π,ι}) for all τ, and π′_{v_{St}} an unramified twist of Steinberg.
items.note: Template: Clozel–Thorne 2017 Theorem 5.1. Proof: Lemma 6.7 gives a generic prime of the big ordinary Hecke algebra; Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 4.1 and Theorem 5.2 compare R_{D_{1,a}} and R_{D_{1,b}}; Geraghty Lemma 2.25 and Theorem 1.2 produce π″, and Lemma 6.2 with Proposition 5.8 descend.

items.name: Lemma 6.2(1)–(2): Schur and primitive after Y_a-split extensions
items.statement: For a Y_a-split finite CM extension L/F (Y_a chosen so that such L are disjoint from the field cut out by r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}}): (1) r̄|_{G_{L⁺(ζ_p)}} is Schur; (2) r̄|_{G_L} is primitive.

items.name: Lemma 6.2(3)–(4): soluble base changes stay cuspidal
items.statement: (3) If L/F is soluble, the base change of π to L is cuspidal. (4) More generally if L/F_0/F with L/F_0 soluble and Π is RACSDC on GL_n(𝔸_{F_0}) with r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ r̄|_{G_{F_0}}, the base change of Π to L is cuspidal.
items.note: A non-cuspidal cyclic base change would make r_{Π_{F_1},ι} induced (Arthur–Clozel Theorems 4.2, 5.1, Proposition 4.4; Clozel's purity lemma), contradicting primitivity.

items.name: Lemma 6.3: auxiliary places with scalar residual Frobenius
items.statement: There are infinitely many prime-to-S places ṽ_a of F not split in F(ζ_p) with r̄(Frob_{ṽ_a}) scalar.
items.note: Chebotarev with τ = τ_0τ_0^c, ϵ(τ_0)² ≠ 1.

items.name: Deformation data D and Lemma 6.4
items.statement: A deformation datum D = (L, {R_v}_{v∈X}) is a Y_a ∪ S̃_a-split soluble CM L/F with X ⊂ S − S_p and, for v ∈ X, R_v = R(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, r̄|_{G_{L_ṽ}}) (v ∈ R_L), the unipotent ring R^1_v or the Steinberg ring R^{St}_v (q_v ≡ 1 mod p, r̄ trivial); 𝒮_D = (L/L⁺, S_{p,L} ∪ X, …, Λ_L, r̄|_{G_{L⁺}}, ϵ^{1−n}δ^n, {R^Δ_v}_{S_{p,L}} ∪ {R_v}_X) with representing ring R_D. Lemma 6.4: every irreducible component of R_D has dimension ≥ 1 + n[L⁺ : ℚ].
items.note: Thorne 2015 Proposition 3.9 and Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 2.1.7.

items.name: Geraghty's big ordinary Hecke algebras and Proposition 6.5
items.statement: For a deformation datum D: U_D and the smooth 𝒪[U_D]-module M_D (lattices in ι^{−1}λ̃(ṽ, Θ_ṽ, n)^∨ on q_ṽ at R-places, Iwahori level with trivial coefficients at R^1/R^{St} places), U(D, c) with Iw_ṽ(c, c) at p and K_ṽ(1) at ṽ_a, 𝕋^{ord}(D, c) ⊂ End S^{ord}(U(D, c), M_D) generated by the T^j_w and diamond operators, 𝕋^{ord}(D) = lim_c 𝕋^{ord}(D, c) and H^{ord}(D) = lim_c Hom(S^{ord}(U(D, c), M_D), 𝒪), with Geraghty's Λ_L-algebra structure. Proposition 6.5: H^{ord}(D) is a finite free Λ_L-module and 𝕋^{ord}(D), if non-zero, a finite faithful Λ_L-algebra.
items.note: As Geraghty Proposition 2.20 and Corollary 2.21 (U(D, 1) sufficiently small).

items.name: Lemma 6.6: the map from the deformation ring to the Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let 𝕋_D = 𝕋^{ord}(D)_{m_D} (m_D generated by m_{Λ_L} and T^j_w − q_w^{j(j−1)/2}tr ∧^j r̄(Frob_w)) and P_D ⊂ R_D the Λ_L-subalgebra generated by characteristic-polynomial coefficients (R_D finite over P_D, Thorne 2015 Propositions 3.26, 3.29). If R_v ≠ R^{St}_v for all v ∈ X, there is a natural surjection P_D → 𝕋_D of Λ_L-algebras; J_D denotes its kernel.
items.note: As Thorne 2015 Proposition 4.12, via Galois representations r_σ over rings A_c (Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemmas 2.1.5, 2.1.7).

items.name: Lemma 6.7: a generic prime unramified outside p
items.statement: There is a deformation datum D_1 = (L_1, ∅) with 𝕋_{D_1} ≠ 0 and a generic prime p_1 ⊂ R_{D_1} of dimension 1 and characteristic p with J_{D_1} ⊂ p_1 and r_{p_1}|_{G_{L_1,v_{St}}} trivial.
items.note: Proof: an R̃ ∪ Y_a ∪ {ṽ_a}-split soluble L_0 with d_{R_i,L_0} > n + n² (cyclic M_d as in Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 7.1; Maire Proposition 19), Theorem 1.4 and Theorem 5.7 at L_0, then L_1 where the types become unramified (Proposition 1.22(4)) and Thorne 2015 Proposition 4.18.

items.name: The CM newform σ_0 of weight 5 and level Γ_1(4)
items.statement: σ_0 is the cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of the normalised newform f_0 = q − 4q² + 16q⁴ − 14q⁵ − 64q⁸ + ⋯ of level Γ_1(4) and weight 5, the automorphic induction from K = ℚ(i) of the unramified Hecke character of ∞-type (4, 0). For p ≡ 1 mod 4, σ_0 is ι-ordinary, r_{σ_0,ι} ≅ Ind^{G_ℚ}_{G_K}ψ and det r_{σ_0,ι} = δ_{K/ℚ}ϵ^{−4}.

items.name: Theorem 7.1: residually CM symmetric powers with a Steinberg place
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3, p ≡ 1 mod 48n!, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ, q ≠ p a prime, X_0 a finite set of places of K prime to 2pq and ω : G_K → Q̄_p^× de Rham with ωω^c = ϵ³ and ω unramified on X_0. Then there are an X_0-split soluble CM extension F/K and a RACSDC ι-ordinary Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) with (a) r̄_{Π,ι} ≅ ω̄^{n−1}|_{G_F} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_F}, (b) HT_τ(r_{Π,ι}) = HT_τ(ω^{n−1}|_{G_F} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_F}) for all τ, and (c) Π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg at some v | q.
items.note: Odd n is Proposition 7.4; n = 2^r m follows by induction on r from Anastassiades–Thorne Theorem 5.1 applied to π_0 = π_1 ⊞ π_2 with r_{π_0} ≅ ω^{2n−1} ⊗ Sym^{2n−1}r_{σ_0}. Remark 7.5: for n a power of 2, Anastassiades–Thorne alone suffices.

items.name: Lemma 7.2: properties of the residual symmetric powers
items.statement: Let n ≥ 3, p ≡ 1 mod 48n!, ω de Rham with ωω^c = ϵ³, F/K finite CM linearly disjoint from the extension of K(ζ_p) cut out by r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_{K(ζ_p)}}, and χ_i = ω̄^{n−1} ⊗ ψ̄^{n−i}(ψ̄^c)^{i−1}, ρ̄ = ⊕χ_i ≅ ω̄^{n−1} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{σ_0,ι}|_{G_K}. Then (1) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1; (2) ψ̄/ψ̄^c|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has order > 2n(n − 1) and χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} order > 2n; (3) χ_iχ_i^c = ϵ^{1−n}; (4) ζ_p ∉ F^{ker ad ρ̄} and F ⊄ F⁺(ζ_p); (5) ρ̄|_{G_F} is primitive.

items.name: Corollary 7.3: a weight-5 form with automorphic symmetric power
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 there is a cuspidal σ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 5, unramified away from 2 and a prime q ≡ 3 mod 4, with σ_2 ≅ i^{GL_2}_{B_2}χ_1 ⊗ χ_2 (χ_1 unramified, χ_2 of conductor 4), σ_q an unramified twist of Steinberg, and Sym^{n−1}r_{σ,ι} automorphic for every p and ι.
items.note: Proof: q ≡ 3 mod 4, q ≡ −1 mod p; level raising for GL_2 (Diamond 1989 Corollary 6.9); Theorem 7.1; Allen–Newton–Thorne Theorem 6.1 (hypotheses from Lemma 7.2) and soluble descent.

items.name: Level raising for GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) (Diamond 1989; Diamond–Taylor 1994) and Edixhoven's ordinarity criterion
items.statement: Diamond 1989 Corollary 6.9 raises the level of a form at a prime q satisfying the level-raising congruence to an unramified Steinberg twist at q; Diamond–Taylor 1994 Theorem A produces forms with prescribed supercuspidal or Steinberg components at non-optimal levels with the same residual representation; a form with reducible residual representation at p, Hodge–Tate weights (0, 8k) and p > 8k is ι-ordinary (Edixhoven 1992 Theorem 2.6).
items.locator: §7, proofs of Corollary 7.3 and Proposition 7.4, pp. 96, 98–99
items.note: Imported GL_2 inputs. The atlas has the Ihara lemma (ModularCurvesPartII R14.4) and level lowering (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2) but no level-raising theorem; CT17's Part II records the same gap.

items.name: Proposition 7.4: Theorem 7.1 for odd n
items.statement: Theorem 7.1 holds when n = 2k + 1 is odd.
items.note: Proof by induction on odd n: Chebotarev primes q_1 (split in K, > n, q_1 a primitive 6th root of unity mod p, Frobenius ratios q_1^{±1} on Ind ψ̄^{2k} and a primitive 12k-th root on Ind ψ̄), q_2 ≡ −1 and q_3 (primitive (n − 2)th root); real quadratic M_1, M_2, M_3; a GL_2 form τ (Diamond–Taylor) Steinberg at q_1 and supercuspidal at q_2; the inductive π on GL_{n−2}; Proposition 5.8 (fixed-type rings, Shotton Definition 3.5), Theorem 4.1, the stronger property at q_1, L_1 = L_0K (Arthur–Clozel Theorem 4.2) and Theorem 6.1.

items.name: Level raising for GL_{2n} of unitary type (Anastassiades–Thorne, Theorem 5.1)
items.statement: Given a RACSDC ι-ordinary π_0 = π_1 ⊞ π_2 on GL_{2n}(𝔸_F) with π_i ≅ St_n(ξ_i) at a place v, ι^{−1}ξ_1/ξ_2(ϖ_v) ≡ q_v^n mod m, and r̄ not a twist of 1 ⊕ ϵ^{−1} ⊕ ⋯, there are a soluble X_0-split quadratic CM F′/F and a RACSDC ι-ordinary π′ of GL_{2n}(𝔸_{F′}) with r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π_0,ι}|_{G_{F′}}, the same weight, and an unramified twist of Steinberg at a place above v.
items.note: Imported from Anastassiades–Thorne, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu (2021); it passes from Sym^{n−1} to Sym^{2n−1}.

items.name: Proposition 8.2: symmetric powers with n-regular refinements at ramified primes
items.statement: Let π be cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2, not CM, with an n-regular accessible refinement at every prime where it is ramified. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every ι.
items.note: Proof by induction on the number of primes dividing the conductor: at a ramified p, move along the tame level M, p-adic eigencurve (avoiding the closed set of Lemma 2.35) to a classical π′ of level prime to p, then Theorem 2.33 (ordinary or non-ordinary case).

items.name: Proposition 8.3: a congruence to a form with n-regular refinements
items.statement: Let π be cuspidal of weight k ≥ 2 without CM, with non-trivial Jacquet module at every l.
