There are p, ι and π′ cuspidal of weight k with (1) p > max(2(n + 1), (n − 1)k); (2) r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) ⊇ a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_p); (3) π_p, π′_p unramified; (4) r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}; (5) every π′_l has non-trivial Jacquet module, and every accessible refinement of π′_l is n-regular where π′_l is ramified.
items.note: Proof by Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching (Kisin Proposition 3.2.5; Thorne 2016 Definition 5.6, Theorem 5.9, Propositions 5.10, 6.5, Lemma 6.8; Khare–Thorne Corollary 2.7, Lemma 2.8; Thorne 2012 Lemma 6.10): if every congruent form failed n-regularity the patched module would live on the codimension-one quotient by I = ∏I_l, contradicting dim H_∞ = 4|T| + q_0. Weston's unobstructedness and Diamond–Taylor Lemma 11 choose p and q_a.

items.name: Lemma 8.4: the non-regular locus of a local lifting ring is a principal divisor
items.statement: For l ∈ S − {p} and a Frobenius lift φ_l there is a principal ideal I_l ⊂ R_l (the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of Sym^{n−1}r_l^{univ}(φ_l)) such that a Q̄_p-point f has eigenvalues α_l, β_l of ρ_f(φ_l) with (α_l/β_l)^i = 1 for some 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1 iff f(I_l) = 0, and dim R_l/I_l < dim R_l.
items.note: Uses that π_l has non-trivial Jacquet module, R_l formally smooth of relative dimension 3, and Gee 2011 Proposition 2.1.5.

items.name: Patching data for modular curves with Fontaine–Laffaille condition at p
items.statement: The deformation problem 𝒮 = (ρ̄, χ, S, {𝒪}, {D_v}) (Fontaine–Laffaille lifts of determinant χ at p, all lifts elsewhere), H = H¹(Y_{U_1(Mq_a)}, Sym^{k−2}𝒪²) with Hecke algebra 𝕋^S and R_𝒮 → 𝕋^S_m surjective, Taylor–Wiles sets Q_N (q ≡ 1 mod p^N, distinct Frobenius eigenvalues, |Q_N| = q_0), Δ_Q, augmented problems 𝒮_Q, H_Q free over 𝒪[Δ_Q] with H_Q ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ H_m, framed rings R^T and presentations A^T_𝒮[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R_{𝒮^T_{Q_N}} with g = q_0 + |T| − 1.
items.note: Auxiliary levels and freeness are GL2ModularityLifting R22.2, arithmetic patching R22.3.

items.name: Soluble base change and descent for GL_n (Arthur–Clozel)
items.statement: Cyclic base change and automorphic induction for GL_n and the resulting soluble descent: if ρ|_{G_F} is automorphic for a soluble extension F/ℚ and irreducible, then ρ is automorphic.
items.locator: §2, proof of Theorem 2.33, p. 59; §6, Lemma 6.2; §7, pp. 97, 101
items.note: ML.5 registers cyclic base change and automorphic induction.

routes.title: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: analytic continuation of symmetric power functoriality along eigenvarieties
routes.brief: Build on Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions), whose ML.3 plans Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy as an endpoint but no layer plans the method that proves it. This Part II owns the first half of that method: moving automorphy of symmetric powers along irreducible components of eigenvarieties. Source: Newton–Thorne, 'Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021)). Its sequel (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B) and the Hilbert modular case (Newton–Thorne, Ann. of Math. 203 (2026)) should extend this Part II. Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 2.33: let (π_0, χ_0), (π′_0, χ′_0) be refined cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) whose points z_0, z′_0 of the tame level N, p-adic eigencurve lie on a common irreducible component, and n ≥ 2. If either (1) χ_0 is numerically non-critical and n-regular, (2) χ′_0 is n-regular, (3) the Zariski closures of r_{π_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) and r_{π′_0,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) contain SL_2 and (4) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic; or (1ord) χ_0 is ordinary, (2ord) π_0, π′_0 are not CM and (3ord) Sym^{n−1}r_{π_0,ι} is automorphic — then Sym^{n−1}r_{π′_0,ι} is automorphic. Theorem 3.1 (Theorem D): if Sym^{n−1} of one everywhere unramified cuspidal π_0 of weight ≥ 2 is automorphic, then so is Sym^{n−1} of every everywhere unramified cuspidal π of weight ≥ 2. Proposition 8.2: if π is non-CM of weight ≥ 2 with an n-regular accessible refinement at every ramified prime, Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic. Proposition 8.3 (congruences to forms with n-regular refinements). Together with Theorem E (owned by SymmetricPowersByUnitaryLevelRaising) these prove Theorems A and B, which ML.3 exports. Layers: (1) Lemma 2.2 (analytic continuation along irreducible components, after Conrad) and the rigid spaces of conjugate self-dual pseudocharacters with their absolutely irreducible loci, Azumaya algebras and tangent spaces (Lemmas 2.12–2.14); (2) the global trianguline tangent bound (Proposition 2.11), with the vanishing of adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer groups (Newton–Thorne, JEMS) as an imported theorem and Allen's genericity notion; (3) symmetric power maps σ_n between pseudocharacter and character spaces, n-regular refinements (Definition 2.23), Theorem 2.24 (non-critical case), Theorem 2.27 (ordinary case), Corollary 2.28 and Lemma 2.29; (4) on the Coleman–Mazur eigencurve: the twin map and Lemma 2.32, Lemma 2.34 (trivialising families of characters over CM fields), the base-change morphism to a definite unitary eigenvariety and Theorem 2.33, and Lemma 2.35 (the bad locus is Zariski closed); (5) the 2-adic eigencurve at the boundary of weight space — Buzzard–Kilford's decomposition ℰ_0(b) = ⊔X_i with slope i·v(w) (Theorem 3.2) as an imported theorem, with the design job deciding whether it belongs as a later layer of PadicFamilies — and the ping-pong Lemmas 3.3–3.7 with Theorem 3.1; (6) killing ramification: Proposition 8.2, the Taylor–Wiles–Kisin argument of Proposition 8.3 with Lemma 8.4 (the non-regular locus is a principal divisor of the local lifting ring), and the final step of Theorem 8.1 through BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1. Use the corrected statements of sourceIssues E1 (Lemma 3.3: z′ ∈ X_{i′}) and E3 (g = q_0 + |T| − 1 in the proof of Proposition 8.3). Imports: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions (PadicFamilies: L2 and L2a for the eigencurve, Buzzard's construction and Coleman classicality); Automorphic Galois Representations PartII (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII: AG2.2, AG2.3, AG2.5); Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison: ET.7a for unitary base change and descent); ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 (soluble descent) and ML.3 (endpoints); Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants: IHG.0–IHG.1); Global Galois deformation rings (GlobalGaloisDeformations: R04.1, G7); Local Galois deformation rings and their components (LocalGaloisDeformationRings: L7 for Fontaine–Laffaille); GL₂ Modularity Lifting (GL2ModularityLifting: R22.2–R22.3 for patching). Coordinate with the pending candidates that own the neighbouring material rather than re-planning it: Completed cohomology and p-adic local–global compatibility, Part II: eigenvarieties, classicality and companion constituents (LocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIEigenvarietyCompanions — Emerton's unitary eigenvariety and Lemma 2.30); The trianguline variety and its local model (TriangulineVarietyAndItsLocalModel — local trianguline deformation theory); Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: polarized automorphy lifting and finiteness of deformation rings (PolarizedAutomorphyLifting — BLGGT14); and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions's Part II SymmetricPowersByUnitaryLevelRaising (Theorem E).
routes.reason: ML.3 plans the endpoints (Theorems A, B, Corollary C) but not their proof, and the atlas has no layer on functoriality along eigenvarieties. The pending candidates are adjacent but aimed elsewhere. Clozel–Thorne's Part II is a different method (level raising). Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen's eigenvariety Part II builds eigenvarieties, classicality and companion points for local–global compatibility, not symmetric-power transfer between eigenvarieties of different groups. The trianguline variety owner is purely local. The Buzzard–Kilford/ping-pong argument and the killing of ramification are specific to symmetric powers. A Part II in ML's direction, importing those owners, is the home that Newton–Thorne II and the Hilbert case can extend.

Newton–Thorne, 'Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021)), is the second source: its Part II ('Raising the level') produces, for every n, a level-one form with automorphic Sym^{n−1}. Final theorems added: Theorem 7.6 (Theorem E) — for n ≥ 3 there is an everywhere unramified cuspidal π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight ≥ 2 with Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} automorphic; Theorem 7.1 — for p ≡ 1 mod 48n!, q ≠ p, X_0 and ω with ωω^c = ϵ³, an X_0-split soluble CM F/ℚ(i) and a RACSDC ι-ordinary Π with r̄_Π ≅ ω̄^{n−1} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{σ_0} (σ_0 the CM newform of weight 5 and level Γ_1(4)), the same Hodge–Tate weights and an unramified Steinberg twist above q; Theorem 4.1 — level raising on the definite unitary group in n = 2k + 1 variables to the types λ(v, θ, n), λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n) at auxiliary places T_1, T_2, T_3; Theorem 6.1 — level raising to Steinberg by the Galois deformation theory of residually reducible representations. routes.brief: This route coalesces with LocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIEigenvarietyCompanions, proposed by PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 and extended by PAPER-DING-25; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. Newton–Thorne (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) §2.17–2.18) adds the eigenvariety ℰ_n of a definite unitary group built from Emerton's locally analytic Jacquet functor without Iwahori restriction at p. Its ingredients are: accessible refinements and Lemma 2.18; the characters ν(π, χ) and j_n with numerically non-critical refinements; Lemmas 2.19–2.20; and Proposition 2.22 (reduced, finite over 𝒯_n, equidimensional with open image of components, Zariski-dense accumulating classical points, Emerton's classicality, Hecke surjectivity and boundedness, via the spectral variety). It also adds the pseudocharacter T_n with the closed immersion i_n; Lemma 2.26 (the Hida-ordinary locus is open and closed and finite over weight space); and Lemma 2.30 — a point of ℰ_n with locally algebraic weight, all of whose local triangulations are non-critical, is classical — proved by excluding companion points with the Orlik–Strauch functors and Breuil's adjunction. Note that Newton–Thorne rely on the published version of Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen 2017 Lemme 2.11, the arXiv version being restricted to crystalline representations. The analytic continuation of symmetric powers that consumes this is the Part II SymmetricPowersByAnalyticContinuation.

Newton–Thorne (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) §2.3.1, §2.11.1) contributes local trianguline deformation theory over arbitrary F_ṽ/ℚ_p in the Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao formalism. It adds: triangulations of given parameter, ordinary and regular parameters, and the spaces 𝒯_v^{reg} and 𝒲_v; uniqueness for regular parameters (Lemma 2.4); the trianguline deformation functor and H¹_tri (Proposition 2.6, after Bellaïche–Chenevier and Nakamura); de Rham-ness of fixed-weight deformations (Lemma 2.7); the numerical criterion for non-critical triangulations of de Rham representations (Lemma 2.8, Definition 2.9); the triangulations of two-dimensional de Rham representations (Example 2.10); and the local trianguline locus with its tangent space (Proposition 2.15). It also records Hellmann's argument (Remark 2.16) that KPX Theorem 6.3.9 holds for the standard notion of Zariski density.
routes.reason: The pending owner of trianguline deformations and the trianguline variety; these items are its local foundations.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations
routes.brief: This route coalesces with SmoothRepresentationsPartII, proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. Newton–Thorne (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) §§1.8, 1.17) use depth-zero types. They add: Moy–Prasad's depth-zero unrefined minimal K-types (p, σ) for a parahoric of U_n with the compact-induction and containment theorems (Proposition 1.14, from Moy–Prasad 1996 Proposition 6.6 and Theorem 6.11); Henniart's explicit unramified Langlands–Kazhdan correspondence for the Deligne–Lusztig type λ̃(ṽ, Θ) of GL_{n_1} (Proposition 1.18); and the containment criteria of Propositions 1.19–1.20 for GL_n, the latter for a pair (q_ṽ, λ̃(ṽ, Θ, n)) that is not a type.
routes.reason: The pending types Part II owns Moy–Prasad depth and types; these are general statements about them, reused by the level-raising Part II.

routes.title: Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: polarized automorphy lifting and finiteness of deformation rings
routes.brief: This route coalesces with PolarizedAutomorphyLifting, proposed by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25; keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. Newton–Thorne (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021) §§1.23, 5, 6) add three things. (1) Hecke operators, Iwahori level and ordinary parts for definite unitary groups, and Geraghty's big ordinary Hecke algebras with Proposition 6.5. (2) The residually reducible deformation theory of §5: primitivity (Lemma 5.1); finiteness of ordinary deformation rings with residual representation a sum of characters (Theorem 5.2); Lemma 5.3; Corollaries 5.4–5.5; the dimension bound for the reducible locus (Proposition 5.6); generic primes in large quotients (Theorem 5.7); and automorphic lifts of prescribed types from residual automorphy over a soluble extension (Proposition 5.8, after Bellovin–Gee Theorem 5.2.1). (3) The imported Allen–Newton–Thorne 2020 and Thorne 2015 theorems, BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 and Lemma A.2.5. Clozel–Thorne's extraction already proposed that Thorne 2015 could live here; Newton–Thorne's §5 is its natural continuation.
routes.reason: The pending owner of polarized automorphy lifting and finiteness of deformation rings on definite unitary groups; Newton–Thorne's §5 proves finiteness in the residually reducible case with the same tools.
